bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第204卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 204
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 204

sentences.zh: 卷第二百四

translations.literal: Roll number two hundred four
translations.idiomatic: Volume Two Hundred Four

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十】 起強圉大淵獻，盡重光單閼，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records Twenty] beginning Qiangyu Dayuanxian, ending Chongguang Danque, altogether five years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records Twenty] From the year Qiangyu Dayuanxian through Chongguang Danque, five years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，閏正月，丁卯，封皇子成美為恆王，隆基為楚王，隆范為衛王，隆業為趙王。

translations.literal: Spring, intercalary first month, day dingmao, enfeoffed imperial sons Chengmei as Prince of Heng, Longji as Prince of Chu, Longfan as Prince of Wei, Longye as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the intercalary first month, on the day dingmao, the court enfeoffed the imperial sons: Chengmei as Prince of Heng, Longji as Prince of Chu, Longfan as Prince of Wei, and Longye as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，突厥骨篤祿等寇昌平，命左鷹揚大將軍黑齒常之帥諸軍討之。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingchen, Tujue Gudulu and others raided Changping; ordered Left Flying Hawk Grand General Heichi Changzhi to lead the armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingchen, the Turkic chieftain Gudulu and his allies raided Changping. The court ordered Left Flying Hawk Grand General Heichi Changzhi to take command of the troops and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙丑，納言韋思謙以太中大夫致仕。

translations.literal: Third month, day yichou, Censor-in-Chief Wei Siqian retired with the rank of Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day yichou, Censor-in-Chief Wei Siqian retired from office with the honorary title of Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，命蘇良嗣留守西京。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, ordered Su Liangsi to remain and guard the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Su Liangsi was appointed to remain behind and administer the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 時尚方監裴匪躬檢校京苑，將鬻苑中蔬果以收其利。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Palace Ateliers Pei Feigong was overseeing the capital gardens, intending to sell the fruits and vegetables in the gardens to reap profit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Feigong, Director of the Palace Ateliers, was supervising the capital imperial gardens and planned to sell their produce for profit.

sentences.zh: 良嗣曰：「昔公儀休相魯，猶能拔葵、去織婦，未聞萬乘之主鬻蔬果也。」

translations.literal: Liangsi said: "In the past Gong Yi Xiu served as minister of Lu, yet could pull up melons and dismiss a weaving woman; one has never heard of a lord of ten thousand chariots selling fruits and vegetables."
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi said, "Even Gongyi Xiu, when he served as prime minister of Lu, pulled up his melon patch and sent away a woman who wove for him rather than compromise his integrity — yet we have never heard of a sovereign selling garden produce for profit."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，裴居道為納言。

translations.literal: Day renxu, Pei Judao became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu, Pei Judao was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，夏官侍郎京兆張光輔為鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingyin, Summer Office Vice Minister Zhang Guangfu of Jingzhao became Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister and co-equal with chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day bingyin, Zhang Guangfu of Jingzhao, Vice Minister of the Summer Office, was made Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister and appointed co-equal with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品劉禕之竊謂鳳閣舍人永年賈大隱曰：「太后既廢昏立明，安用臨朝稱制！

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister, co-equal with Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Third Rank Liu Yizhi secretly said to Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Jia Dayin of Yongnian: "The Empress Dowager has already deposed the dim and established the bright — what need is there to hold court and exercise regency!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi, Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister and co-equal with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Third Rank, whispered to Jia Dayin of Yongnian, a Phoenix Pavilion Attendant: "The Empress Dowager has already removed an unfit ruler and set a worthy one on the throne — why must she still hold court and rule by decree?

sentences.zh: 不如返政，以安天下之心。」

translations.literal: Better to return government, to settle the hearts of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: She ought to return power to the throne and put the empire at ease."

sentences.zh: 大隱密奏之，太后不悅，謂左右曰：「禕之我所引，乃復叛我！」

translations.literal: Dayin secretly memorialized this; the Empress Dowager was displeased, and said to those beside her: "Yizhi was my own appointee, yet he turns against me again!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dayin secretly reported this to the Empress Dowager. She was displeased and said to those around her, "Yizhi was my own appointee, yet he turns against me again!"

sentences.zh: 或誣禕之受歸誠州都督孫萬榮金，又與許敬宗妾有私，太后命肅州刺史王本立推之。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Yizhi for receiving gold from Guichengzhou Protector-General Sun Wanrong, and also having illicit relations with Xu Jingzong's concubine; the Empress Dowager ordered Suzhou Prefect Wang Benli to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then accused Yizhi of taking bribes from Sun Wanrong, military commissioner of Guicheng Prefecture, and of having an affair with a concubine of Xu Jingzong. The Empress Dowager ordered Wang Benli, prefect of Suzhou, to investigate.

sentences.zh: 本立宣敕示之，禕之曰：「不經鳳閣鸞台，何名為敕！」

translations.literal: Benli proclaimed the edict and showed it to him; Yizhi said: "Not passing through Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace — how can it be called an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Benli presented the edict. Yizhi replied, "An order that has not passed through the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace is no edict at all!"

sentences.zh: 太后大怒，以為拒捍制使；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was greatly angered, taking it as resisting and defying the edict-bearer;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage and charged him with defying an imperial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Day gengwu, granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 禕之初下獄，睿宗為之上疏申理，親友皆賀之，禕之曰：「經乃所以速吾死也。」

translations.literal: When Yizhi first entered prison, Ruizong wrote a memorial on his behalf to plead his case; relatives and friends all congratulated him; Yizhi said: "The memorial is precisely what will hasten my death."
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi was first thrown into prison, Emperor Ruizong submitted a memorial pleading his case. Friends and relatives congratulated him on this support, but Yizhi said, "That memorial is what will hasten my death."

sentences.zh: 臨刑，沐浴，神色自若，自草謝表，立成數紙。

translations.literal: At execution, he bathed, his expression composed as ever, and himself drafted a memorial of thanks, completing several sheets at once.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, he bathed himself, remained perfectly composed, and drafted a final memorial of thanks to the throne, finishing several pages in a single sitting.

sentences.zh: 麟台郎郭翰、太子文學周思均稱歎其文。

translations.literal: Unicorn Terrace Gentleman Guo Han and Crown Prince Literary Scholar Zhou Sijun praised and marveled at his writing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Han, a Unicorn Terrace secretary, and Zhou Sijun, a literary tutor to the Crown Prince, marveled at the quality of his prose.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，左遷翰巫州司法，思鈞播州司倉。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager heard of it, and demoted Han to judicial officer of Wuzhou, Sijun to storekeeper of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager learned of this, she demoted Guo Han to judicial officer in Wuzhou and Zhou Sijun to granary clerk in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，魏玄同檢校納言。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renchen, Wei Xuantong acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day renchen, Wei Xuantong was appointed acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嶺南俚戶舊輸半課，交趾都護劉延祐使之全輸，俚戶不從，延祐誅其魁首。

translations.literal: Lingnan Liao households formerly paid half the tax levy; Jiaozhi Protector-General Liu Yanyou made them pay in full; the Liao households would not comply, and Yanyou executed their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingnan the Liao people had long paid only half the regular tax. Liu Yanyou, protector-general of Jiaozhi, demanded payment in full. When they refused, he put their ringleaders to death.

sentences.zh: 其黨李思慎等作亂，攻破安南府城，殺延祐。

translations.literal: Their faction Li Sishan and others rebelled, broke through Annan prefectural city, killed Yanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sishan and his followers rose in revolt, stormed the seat of Annan Prefecture, and killed Liu Yanyou.

sentences.zh: 桂州司馬曹玄靜將兵討思慎等，斬之。

translations.literal: Guizhou Assistant Commander Cao Xuanjing led troops to attack Sishan and others, beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xuanjing, assistant military commander of Guizhou, marched against them, defeated Li Sishan and his band, and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 突厥骨篤祿、元珍寇朔州；

translations.literal: Tujue Gudulu and Yuan Zhen raided Shuozhou;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks Gudulu and Yuan Zhen raided Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 遣燕然道大總管黑齒常之擊之，以右鷹揚大將軍李多祚為之副，大破突厥於黃花堆，追奔四十餘里，突厥皆散走磧北。

translations.literal: Dispatched Yenan Circuit Grand Commander Heichi Changzhi to attack them, with Right Flying Hawk Grand General Li Duozhuo as his deputy; greatly defeated the Turks at Yellow Flower Mound, pursued the rout forty-odd li; the Turks all scattered and fled north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Heichi Changzhi, grand commander of the Yenan circuit, to meet them, with Right Flying Hawk Grand General Li Duozhuo as his second. At Yellow Flower Mound they routed the Turks and chased the fleeing enemy more than forty li, until the invaders broke up and fled across the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 多祚世為靺鞨酋長，以軍功得入宿衛。

translations.literal: Duozhuo for generations had been a Mohe chieftain, and through military merit gained entry into palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozhuo came from a long line of Mohe chieftains and had won a place in the imperial guard through military service.

sentences.zh: 黑齒常之每得賞賜，皆分將士；

translations.literal: Heichi Changzhi whenever he received rewards and gifts, all shared them with officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Heichi Changzhi received imperial rewards, he divided them among his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 有善馬為軍士所損，官屬請笞之，常之曰：「奈何以私馬笞官兵乎！」

translations.literal: There was a fine horse damaged by soldiers; subordinate officials requested to whip them; Changzhi said: "How can one use a private horse to whip officers and soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: When a good horse of his was injured by some soldiers, his staff urged that they be flogged. Changzhi said, "How can I punish my officers and men over a private horse of mine!"

sentences.zh: 卒不問。

translations.literal: In the end he did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 九月，己卯，虢州人楊初成詐稱郎將，矯制於都市募人迎廬陵王於房州；

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jimao, Guo Prefecture man Yang Chucheng falsely claimed to be a commandant, forged an edict in the market city to recruit men to welcome the Prince of Luling from Fang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day jimao, a man of Guo Prefecture named Yang Chucheng impersonated a military commandant and, forging an imperial order, recruited men in the marketplace to go bring the Prince of Luling back from Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered, he suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚子，右監門衛中郎將爨寶璧與突厥骨篤祿、元珍戰，全軍皆沒，寶璧輕騎遁歸。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengzi, Right Supervisor of the Gate Guard Middle General Cuan Baobi fought with Tujue Gudulu and Yuan Zhen; the entire army was lost; Baobi fled back on a light horse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day gengzi, Cuan Baobi, a middle general of the Right Gate Guard, engaged Gudulu and Yuan Zhen of the Turks. His whole force was wiped out, and he escaped home with only a handful of light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 寶璧見黑齒常之有功，表請窮追餘寇。

translations.literal: Baobi saw Heichi Changzhi had meritorious achievement, memorialized requesting to pursue the remnant raiders to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Heichi Changzhi's recent success, Baobi memorialized the throne asking permission to hunt down the remaining enemy to the last man.

sentences.zh: 詔與常之計議，遙為聲援。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to consult with Changzhi and provide distant support.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to coordinate with Changzhi and lend distant support.

sentences.zh: 寶璧欲專其功，不待常之，引精兵萬三千人先行，出塞二千餘里，掩擊其部落；

translations.literal: Baobi wished to monopolize the merit, did not wait for Changzhi, led elite troops of thirteen thousand men to go ahead, went beyond the frontier two thousand-odd li, and launched a surprise attack on their tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Eager to claim all the credit himself, Baobi did not wait for Changzhi. He marched ahead with thirteen thousand picked troops, crossed more than two thousand li beyond the frontier, and fell upon the Turkic encampments by surprise.

sentences.zh: 既至，又先遣人告之，使得嚴備，與戰，遂敗。

translations.literal: Having arrived, he again first sent men to inform them, enabling them to prepare defenses strictly; they joined battle, and he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he sent word ahead of his arrival, giving the enemy time to prepare. When battle was joined, he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 太后誅寶璧；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager executed Baobi;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had Baobi executed.

sentences.zh: 改骨篤祿曰不卒祿。

translations.literal: Changed Gudulu's name to Buzulu.
translations.idiomatic: She mockingly renamed Gudulu "Buzulu" — "He Who Does Not Die in Battle."

sentences.zh: 命魏玄同留守西京。

translations.literal: Ordered Wei Xuantong to remain and guard the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuantong was ordered to remain behind and administer the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣又使人誣李孝逸自云「名中有兔，兔，月中物，當有天分。」

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi again sent men to slander Li Xiaoyi as saying of himself: "In my name there is the rabbit; the rabbit is a thing of the moon — I ought to have Heaven's portion."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi again had Li Xiaoyi accused of boasting, "The character for 'rabbit' is in my name — and the rabbit belongs to the moon. Surely this means Heaven's mandate is mine."

sentences.zh: 太后以孝逸有功，十一月，戊寅，減死除名，流儋州而卒。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager because Xiaoyi had merit, eleventh month, day wuyin, reduced death and struck his name from the rolls, exiled to Dan Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Xiaoyi had once done the dynasty great service, the Empress Dowager commuted his death sentence to removal from the register of officials and exile to Dan Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 太后欲遣韋待價將兵擊吐蕃，鳳閣侍郎韋方質奏，請如舊制遣御史監軍。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to dispatch Wei Daigi to lead troops to attack Tubo; Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Wei Fangzhi memorialized, requesting according to old institutions to dispatch censor to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager planned to send Wei Daigi to lead troops against Tibet, Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Wei Fangzhi memorialized the throne, urging that censors be sent to supervise the army as in past practice.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「古者名君遣將，閫外之事悉以委之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "In antiquity when celebrated rulers dispatched generals, all matters beyond the gate they fully entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager replied, "In antiquity, when worthy rulers dispatched generals, they entrusted them with full authority over all affairs beyond the gate.

sentences.zh: 比聞御史監軍，軍中事無大小皆須承稟。

translations.literal: Recently one hears censors supervising armies — in the army affairs great and small all must await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have heard that with censors overseeing the armies, no matter in camp, great or small, may be decided without awaiting instructions from above.

sentences.zh: 以下制上，非令典也；

translations.literal: Using the lower to constrain the upper — this is not good institutions;
translations.idiomatic: That is the lower hand controlling the higher — it is no proper precedent.

sentences.zh: 且何以責其有功！」

translations.literal: Moreover, how can one demand merit of them!"
translations.idiomatic: And how, under such conditions, can we hold a general accountable for winning victories?"

sentences.zh: 遂罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下大饑，山東、關內尤甚。

translations.literal: This year, all under Heaven suffered great famine; Shandong and Guannei were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine ravaged the empire; Shandong and the Guanzhong region suffered worst of all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，於神都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟，四時享祀如西廟之儀。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiazi, at Shendu established temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, seasonal offerings and sacrifices like the Western Capital temples' rituals.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day jiazi, temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were established at the Divine Capital, with seasonal rites performed according to the ceremonies used at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 又立崇先廟以享武氏祖考。

translations.literal: Also established the Exalted Ancestors Temple to offer to the Wu clan's forebears.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Exalted Ancestors Temple was also established for sacrifices to the Wu family's forebears.

sentences.zh: 太后命有司議崇先廟室數，司禮博士周悰請為七室，又減唐太廟為五室。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered the relevant offices to discuss the number of chambers for the Exalted Ancestors Temple; Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Zhou Cong requested seven chambers, and also reduced the Tang imperial ancestral temple to five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered the relevant offices to debate how many ancestral chambers the Exalted Ancestors Temple should have. Zhou Cong, an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, proposed seven chambers for it and a corresponding reduction of the Tang imperial temple to five.

sentences.zh: 春官侍郎賈大隱奏：「禮，天子七廟，諸侯五廟，百王不易之義。

translations.literal: Spring Office Vice Minister Jia Dayin memorialized: "By rites, the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples — the principle unchanged through a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dayin, Vice Minister of the Spring Office, submitted a memorial: "By ritual law the Son of Heaven maintains seven ancestral temples and a feudal lord five — a rule no true sovereign has ever overturned.

sentences.zh: 今周悰別引浮議，廣異述文，直崇臨朝權儀，不依國家常度。

translations.literal: Now Zhou Cong separately cites frivolous discussions, expands heterodox interpretations, directly exalting the regent's provisional authority — not following the state's regular norms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cong now cites loose opinions and stretches the texts to serve the Empress Dowager's provisional regency — this ignores the state's settled practice.

sentences.zh: 皇太后親承顧托，光顯大猷，其崇先廟室應如諸侯之數，國家宗廟不應輒有變移。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager personally received the entrustment, illuminating the great design — her Exalted Ancestors Temple chambers ought to be like a feudal lord's number; the state's ancestral temple ought not rashly to have changes and shifts."
translations.idiomatic: Her Majesty personally received the late emperor's trust and has governed with conspicuous wisdom. The Exalted Ancestors Temple should therefore be accorded no more chambers than a feudal lord's allowance. The Tang ancestral temple must not be altered on a whim."

sentences.zh: 太后乃止。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 太宗、高宗之世，屢欲立明堂，諸儒議其制度，不決而止。

translations.literal: In the eras of Taizong and Gaozong, repeatedly wished to establish the Bright Hall; various Confucians debated its system — could not decide and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong and Gaozong the court had repeatedly planned to build the Bright Hall, but the Confucian scholars could never agree on its design, and each time the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及太后稱制，獨與北門學士議其制，不問諸儒。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager exercised regency, alone with the Northern Gate Scholars discussed its system, not consulting the various Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Empress Dowager took power, she discussed the design only with her Northern Gate Scholars and ignored the mainstream scholars entirely.

sentences.zh: 諸儒以為明堂當在國陽丙己之地，三里之外，七里之內。

translations.literal: The various Confucians held that the Bright Hall ought to be in the state's southern yang bingji location, outside three li, within seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Orthodox scholars held that the Bright Hall should stand in the state's due south, in the bing and ji directions, no closer than three li from the palace and no farther than seven.

sentences.zh: 太后以為去宮太遠。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager held that it was too far from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager considered that too distant from the palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，毀乾元殿，於其地作明堂，以僧懷義為之使，凡役數萬人。

translations.literal: Second month, day gengwu, destroyed the Qianyuan Hall, at that site built the Bright Hall, with monk Huaiyi as commissioner — in all conscripted tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day gengwu, the Qianyuan Hall was torn down and the Bright Hall erected in its place. The monk Huaiyi was placed in charge of the work, and tens of thousands of laborers were impressed for the task.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊戌，殺太子通事舍人郝象賢。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wuxu, killed Crown Prince Duty Attendant Hao Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day wuxu, Hao Xiangxian, a duty attendant to the Crown Prince, was executed.

sentences.zh: 像賢，處俊之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was Chujun's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xiangxian was the grandson of Hao Chujun.

sentences.zh: 初，太后有憾於處俊，會奴誣告象賢反，太后命周興鞫之，致象賢族罪。

translations.literal: Initially, the Empress Dowager bore resentment toward Chujun; it happened a slave falsely reported Xiangxian rebelled; the Empress Dowager ordered Zhou Xing to interrogate him, leading to Xiangxian's clan being condemned.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had long resented Hao Chujun. When a household slave falsely accused Hao Xiangxian of treason, she ordered Zhou Xing to investigate and had the entire Hao clan condemned on his charge.

sentences.zh: 像賢家人詣朝堂，訟冤於監察御史樂安任玄殖。

translations.literal: Xiangxian's family members went to the court hall, pleaded innocence before Supervising Censor Ren Xuanzhi of Lean.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian's family went to the audience hall and appealed to Ren Xuanzhi of Lean, a supervising censor, proclaiming his innocence.

sentences.zh: 玄殖奏象賢無反狀，玄殖坐免官。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi memorialized that Xiangxian had no signs of rebellion; Xuanzhi suffered removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xuanzhi submitted a memorial stating that there was no evidence Hao Xiangxian had plotted rebellion. For this he was stripped of his office.

sentences.zh: 像賢臨刑，極口罵太后，發揚宮中隱慝，奪市人柴以擊刑者；

translations.literal: Xiangxian at execution, to the utmost cursed the Empress Dowager, exposed hidden wickedness of the inner palace, seized firewood from market people to strike the executioners;
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground Xiangxian cursed the Empress Dowager without restraint, shouted out the palace's darkest secrets, and snatched firewood from bystanders to hurl at his executioners.

sentences.zh: 金吾兵共格殺之。

translations.literal: Gold Guard soldiers together struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Gold Guard soldiers fell upon him and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太后命支解其屍，發其父祖墳，毀棺焚屍。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered his corpse dismembered, his father and grandfather's tombs opened, coffins destroyed and corpses burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered his body cut to pieces, his father's and grandfathers' graves opened, their coffins destroyed, and their remains burned.

sentences.zh: 自是終太后之世，法官每刑人，先以木丸塞其口。

translations.literal: From this until the end of the Empress Dowager's reign, judicial officers whenever executing men, first used wooden pellets to stop their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: From that day until the end of her reign, executioners routinely stuffed wooden pellets into prisoners' mouths before carrying out a sentence.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣使鑿白石為文曰：「聖母臨人，永昌帝業。」

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi had white stone carved with text saying: "Holy Mother presides over the people, eternal flourishing of the imperial enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi had a piece of white stone inscribed with the words: "The Holy Mother rules the people; the imperial enterprise shall flourish forever."

sentences.zh: 末紫石雜藥物填之。

translations.literal: The end — purple stone mixed with medicaments to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription was then patched over with purple stone and medicaments.

sentences.zh: 庚午，使雍州人唐同泰奉表獻之，稱獲之於洛水。

translations.literal: Day gengwu, had Yongzhou man Tang Tongtai present it in memorial tribute, claiming to have obtained it from the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, a man of Yong Prefecture named Tang Tongtai was sent to present it to the throne with a memorial claiming it had been found in the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 太后喜，命其石曰「寶圖」，擢同泰為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased, named the stone "Treasure Chart," and promoted Tongtai to Irregular Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Empress Dowager named the stone the "Treasure Chart" and promoted Tang Tongtai to the rank of irregular cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰，詔當親拜洛，受「寶圖」；

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuchen, edict that she should personally worship at the Luo, receive the "Treasure Chart";
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wuchen, an edict was issued ordering her to worship at the Luo River in person and receive the Treasure Chart.

sentences.zh: 有事南郊，先謝昊天；

translations.literal: Perform the southern suburban sacrifice, first thank August Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: She was to offer the southern suburban sacrifice and first give thanks to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，御明堂，朝群臣。

translations.literal: When rites were complete, mount the Bright Hall, hold court with the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, she would enter the Bright Hall and hold court with the ministers.

sentences.zh: 命諸州都督、刺史及宗室、外戚以拜洛前十日集神都。

translations.literal: Ordered the various prefectures' military commissioners, prefects, and imperial clansmen and consort kin to assemble at Shendu ten days before the Luo worship.
translations.idiomatic: All regional commanders, prefects, imperial clansmen, and consort relatives were ordered to gather at the Divine Capital ten days before the river ceremony.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，太后加尊號為聖母神皇。

translations.literal: Day yihai, the Empress Dowager added honorific title as Holy Mother Divine Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, the Empress Dowager took the additional honorific title Holy Mother and Divine Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day dinghai, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the new moon, the day dinghai, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，作神皇三璽。

translations.literal: Day renyin, made the Divine Sovereign's three seals.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, the three imperial seals of the Divine Sovereign were cast.

sentences.zh: 東陽大長公主削封邑，並二子徙巫州。

translations.literal: Eastern Yang Grand Senior Princess had fief reduced, together with two sons exiled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Senior Princess of Eastern Yang was stripped of her fief, and she and her two sons were banished to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 公主適度履行，太后以高氏長孫無忌之舅族，故惡之。

translations.literal: The princess had married Du Xingli; the Empress Dowager because the Gaos were elder maternal clan of Zhangsun Wuji, therefore hated her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had married Du Xingli. The Empress Dowager despised her because the Du clan was related by marriage to the Zhangsun family — maternal kin of Zhangsun Wuji.

sentences.zh: 河南道巡撫大使、冬官侍郎狄仁傑以吳、楚多淫祠，奏焚其一千七百餘所，獨留夏禹、吳太伯、季札、伍員四祠。

translations.literal: Henan Circuit Investigation Commissioner, Winter Office Vice Minister Di Renjie because Wu and Chu had many illicit shrines, memorialized burning over seventeen hundred of them, only retaining four shrines: to Xia Yu, Wu Taibo, Jizi, and Wu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie of the Winter Office, investigation commissioner for the Henan circuit, memorialized that Wu and Chu were overrun with illicit shrines. He had more than seventeen hundred of them burned down, sparing only the temples to Yu the Great, Wu Taibo, Jizi, and Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingsi, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day dingsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 更命「寶圖」為「天授聖圖」；

translations.literal: Renamed the "Treasure Chart" as "Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart";
translations.idiomatic: The Treasure Chart was renamed the Heaven-Bestowed Holy Chart.

sentences.zh: 洛水為永昌洛水，封其神為顯聖侯，加特進，禁漁釣，祭祀比四瀆。

translations.literal: The Luo River as Eternal Prosperity Luo River, ennobled its spirit as Manifest Sage Marquis, added special advance rank, prohibited fishing and angling, sacrifices comparable to the Four Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo River was renamed the Eternal Prosperity Luo River. Its spirit was enfeoffed as Marquis Manifest Sage with the honorary rank of special advancement; fishing was forbidden, and its cult was elevated to the level of the Four Sacred Rivers.

sentences.zh: 名圖所出曰「聖圖泉」，泉側置永昌縣。

translations.literal: Named where the chart emerged as "Holy Chart Spring," beside the spring established Yongchang County.
translations.idiomatic: The spring where the chart had supposedly appeared was named Holy Chart Spring, and Yongchang County was established beside it.

sentences.zh: 又改嵩山為神岳，封其神為天中王，拜太師、使持節、神岳大都督，禁芻牧。

translations.literal: Also changed Song Mountain to Divine Peak, ennobled its spirit as King Mid-Heaven, appointed Grand Preceptor, commissioner bearing the staff of authority, Divine Peak Grand Commander, prohibited grazing and herding.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Song was renamed the Divine Peak. Its spirit was enfeoffed as King of the Central Heaven and given the titles Grand Preceptor, commissioner bearing the staff of authority, and grand commander of the Divine Peak; grazing was forbidden on its slopes.

sentences.zh: 又以先於汜水得瑞石，改汜水為廣武。

translations.literal: Also because previously at Sishui a auspicious stone was obtained, changed Sishui to Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Because an auspicious stone had earlier been found at Sishui, that place was renamed Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 太后潛謀革命，稍除宗室。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager secretly plotted to change the dynasty, gradually removing the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager secretly planned to overturn the dynasty and was steadily purging the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 絳州刺史韓王元嘉、青州刺史霍王元軌、刑州刺史魯王靈夔、豫州刺史越王貞及元嘉子通州刺史黃公譔、元軌子金州刺史江都王緒、虢王鳳子申州刺史東莞公融、靈夔子范陽王藹、貞子博州刺史琅邪王沖，在宗室中皆以才行有美名，太后尤忌之。

translations.literal: Jiang Prefecture Prefect Prince of Han Yuan Jia, Qing Prefecture Prefect Prince of Huo Yuan Gui, Xing Prefecture Prefect Prince of Lu Lingqi, Yu Prefecture Prefect Prince of Yue Zhen, and Yuan Jia's son Tong Prefecture Prefect Duke of Huang Zuan, Yuan Gui's son Jin Prefecture Prefect Prince of Jiangdu Xu, Prince of Guo Feng's son Shen Prefecture Prefect Duke of Dongguan Rong, Lingqi's son Prince of Fanyang Ai, Zhen's son Bo Prefecture Prefect Prince of Langye Chong — among the imperial clan all were famed for virtue and talent; the Empress Dowager especially envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Jia of Han, prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Prince Yuan Gui of Huo, prefect of Qing Prefecture; Prince Lingqi of Lu, prefect of Xing Prefecture; Prince Zhen of Yue, prefect of Yu Prefecture; Zuan, Duke of Huang and prefect of Tong Prefecture, Yuan Jia's son; Xu, Prince of Jiangdu and prefect of Jin Prefecture, Yuan Gui's son; Rong, Duke of Dongguan and prefect of Shen Prefecture, son of Prince Feng of Guo; Ai, Prince of Fanyang, Lingqi's son; and Chong, Prince of Langye and prefect of Bo Prefecture, Zhen's son — all enjoyed fine reputations among the imperial clansmen for character and ability, and the Empress Dowager resented them above all others.

sentences.zh: 元嘉等內不自安，密有匡復之志。

translations.literal: Yuan Jia and the others inwardly were not at ease, secretly had the resolve to restore the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jia and the others grew uneasy at heart and secretly vowed to restore the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 譔謬為書與貞云：「內人病浸重，當速療之，若至今冬，恐成痼疾。」

translations.literal: Zuan falsely made a letter to Zhen saying: "The inner person is ill and worsening — must quickly treat it; if until this winter, fear becoming a chronic malady."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan forged a letter to Prince Zhen reading, "The patient within grows worse by the day. Treat her quickly — wait until winter and the sickness may become incurable."

sentences.zh: 及太后召宗室朝明堂，諸王因遞相驚曰：「神皇欲於大饗之際，使人告密，盡收宗室，誅之無遺類。」

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager summoned the imperial clan to court at the Bright Hall, the princes consequently passed word to each other in alarm saying: "The Divine Sovereign wishes at the great feast to have men inform secretly, entirely seize the imperial clan, execute them without survivors."
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager summoned the princes to attend court at the Bright Hall, they passed frantic messages among themselves: "The Divine Sovereign intends, during the great assembly, to set informers loose, round up the entire imperial clan, and exterminate every last one of us."

sentences.zh: 譔詐為皇帝璽書與沖云：「朕遭幽縶，諸王宜各發兵救我。」

translations.literal: Zuan falsely made the Emperor's seal letter to Chong saying: "I suffer secret imprisonment — the various princes ought each to raise troops to rescue me."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan forged an imperial edict under the emperor's seal and sent it to Prince Chong: "I am held in secret confinement. Every prince must raise troops at once to rescue me."

sentences.zh: 沖又詐為皇帝璽書云：「神皇欲移李氏社稷，以授武氏。」

translations.literal: Chong again falsely made the Emperor's seal letter saying: "The Divine Sovereign wishes to transfer the Li clan's altars of state, to bestow them on the Wu clan."
translations.idiomatic: Chong in turn forged another imperial edict: "The Divine Sovereign means to take the Li dynasty's throne and give it to the Wu clan."

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，沖召長史蕭德琮等令募兵，分告韓、霍、魯、越及貝州刺史紀王慎，各令起兵共趣神都。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day renyin, Chong summoned Chief Clerk Xiao Decong and others, ordering them to raise troops, and separately notified the Han, Huo, Lu, and Yue [princes], as well as Prince Shen of Ji, Prefect of Beizhou, each ordering them to raise troops together to converge on the Divine Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the renyin day, Prince Chong summoned his chief clerk Xiao Decong and others to recruit soldiers, and dispatched messages to the princes of Han, Huo, Lu, and Yue, as well as Prince Shen of Ji, prefect of Beizhou, instructing each to rise in arms and march on the Divine Capital.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，以左金吾將軍丘神勣為清平道行軍大總管以討之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager heard of it, and appointed Left Golden Crow General Qiu Shenji as Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit Campaign to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager heard of this, she appointed Left Golden Crow General Qiu Shenji grand commander of the Qingping circuit campaign to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 沖募兵得五千餘人，欲渡河取濟州；

translations.literal: Chong raised troops, obtaining more than five thousand men, intending to cross the river and seize Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chong mustered a little over five thousand men and planned to cross the river and take Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 先擊武水，武水令郭務悌詣魏州求救。

translations.literal: First he attacked Wushui; Wushui Magistrate Guo Wuti went to Weizhou to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He struck first at Wushui; its magistrate, Guo Wuti, hurried to Weizhou to beg for relief.

sentences.zh: 莘令馬玄素將兵千七百人中道邀沖，恐力不敵，入武水，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Shen County Magistrate Ma Xuansu led seventeen hundred troops to intercept Chong on the road; fearing his strength was not equal, he entered Wushui, shut the gates, and resisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xuansu, magistrate of Shen County, marched seventeen hundred men to ambush Chong on the road. Finding himself outmatched, he withdrew into Wushui, barred the gates, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 沖推草車塞其南門，因風縱火焚之，欲乘火突入；

translations.literal: Chong pushed hay carts to block its south gate, took advantage of the wind to set fire and burn it, intending to exploit the fire to burst in;
translations.idiomatic: Chong piled hay carts against the south gate, set them ablaze in the wind, and tried to storm the town through the flames;

sentences.zh: 火作而風回，沖軍不得進，由是氣沮。

translations.literal: The fire rose but the wind turned back; Chong's army could not advance — by this their morale was dejected.
translations.idiomatic: The flames leaped up, then the wind shifted; Chong's men could not get forward, and their spirits sank.

sentences.zh: 堂邑董玄寂為衝將兵擊武水，謂人曰：「琅邪王與國家交戰，此乃反也。」

translations.literal: Tangyi native Dong Xuanji, serving as Chong's officer leading troops to attack Wushui, said to people: "The Prince of Langye battles the state — this is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuanji of Tangyi, one of Chong's commanders in the assault on Wushui, told others, "The Prince of Langye is fighting the state itself — this is treason.

sentences.zh: 沖聞之，斬玄寂以徇，眾懼而散入草澤，不可禁止，惟家僮左右數十人在。

translations.literal: Chong heard of it, beheaded Xuanji as a warning; the masses feared and scattered into meadows and marshes, impossible to restrain — only several dozen household servants and attendants remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong heard this, he had Xuanji executed as an example. The troops panicked and fled into the fields and marshes; he could not hold them, and only a few dozen personal servants stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 沖還走博州，戊申，至城門，為守門者所殺，凡起兵七日而敗。

translations.literal: Chong fled back toward Bozhou; on day wushen, when he reached the city gate, he was killed by the gate guards — in all, from raising troops to defeat, seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Chong fled back toward Bozhou. On the wushen day, as he reached the city gate, the guards killed him. His uprising had lasted only seven days.

sentences.zh: 丘神勣至博州，官吏素服出迎，神勣揮刃盡殺之，凡破千餘家。

translations.literal: Qiu Shenji reached Bozhou; officials and clerks in plain white robes came out to welcome him — Shenji waved his blade and killed them all, in all destroying more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Shenji arrived at Bozhou, the local officials came out in mourning dress to welcome him. He cut them down to the last man, and more than a thousand families were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 越王貞聞衝起，亦舉兵於豫州，遣兵陷上蔡。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen of Yue heard Chong had risen, also raised troops at Yuzhou, and dispatched troops to capture Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen of Yue heard that Chong had risen in revolt, he too took up arms in Yuzhou and sent forces to seize Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙辰，命左豹韜大將軍麴崇裕為中軍大總管，岑長倩為後軍大總管，將兵十萬以討之，又命張光輔為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day bingchen, appointed Left Leopard-strap Grand General Qu Chongyu as Grand Commander of the Center Army, Cen Changqian as Grand Commander of the Rear Army, leading a hundred thousand troops to attack him; also appointed Zhang Guangfu as controller of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the bingchen day, the court named Left Leopard-strap Grand General Qu Chongyu commander of the center army and Cen Changqian commander of the rear army, and sent a hundred thousand men against Prince Zhen. Zhang Guangfu was placed in overall command.

sentences.zh: 削貞、沖屬籍，更姓虺氏。

translations.literal: Struck Zhen and Chong from the clan registers, changed their surname to the Hui clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Chong were struck from the imperial registers and given the surname Hui.

sentences.zh: 貞聞沖敗，欲自鎖詣闕謝罪，會所署新蔡令傅延慶募得勇士二千餘人，貞乃宣言於眾曰：「琅邪已破魏、相數州，有兵二十萬，朝夕至矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen heard Chong had been defeated, wished to bind himself and go to the palace to confess guilt; it happened that his appointed Xincai Magistrate Fu Yanqing recruited more than two thousand brave warriors — Zhen then proclaimed to the masses: "Langye has already broken Wei, Xiang, and several prefectures, with two hundred thousand troops — they will arrive within the day.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen learned of Chong's defeat, he meant to put himself in chains and go to the capital to plead guilty. Just then Fu Yanqing, the magistrate of Xincai whom he had appointed, raised more than two thousand fighting men. Zhen told his followers, "The Prince of Langye has already overrun Wei, Xiang, and several neighboring prefectures. He has two hundred thousand soldiers and will be here any day now.

sentences.zh: 發屬縣兵共得五千，分為五營，使汝陽縣丞裴守德等將之，署九品以上官五百餘人。

translations.literal: He mobilized the subordinate counties' troops, altogether obtaining five thousand, divided into five camps, making Ruyang Assistant Prefect Pei Shoude and others lead them; appointed more than five hundred officials of ninth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: He called up the militia of the surrounding counties until he had five thousand men, divided them into five camps under Pei Shoude, assistant magistrate of Ruyang, and others, and installed more than five hundred officials down to the ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 所署官皆受迫脅，莫有鬥志，惟安德與之同謀，貞以其女妻之，署大將軍，委以腹心。

translations.literal: The appointed officials all suffered coercion — none had fighting will; only Shoude shared the plot with him. Zhen gave him his daughter in marriage, appointed him Grand General, and entrusted him as his innermost confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer he appointed had been coerced into service and showed no fight. Only Pei Shoude had truly joined the conspiracy. Zhen married his daughter to him, made him grand general, and relied on him as his closest confidant.

sentences.zh: 貞使道士及僧誦經以求事成，左右及戰士皆帶辟兵符。

translations.literal: Zhen had Daoist priests and monks chant sutras seeking the affair's success; attendants and warriors all wore talismans to avert weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen set Daoists and monks to chanting scriptures for victory, and his attendants and soldiers all wore protective amulets against weapons.

sentences.zh: 麴崇裕等軍至豫州城東四十里，貞遣少子規及裴守德拒戰，兵潰而歸。

translations.literal: Qu Chongyu's and others' army reached forty li east of Yuzhou City; Zhen sent his younger son Gui and Pei Shoude to resist in battle — the troops collapsed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Chongyu's force reached a point forty li east of Yuzhou, Prince Zhen sent his younger son Gui and Pei Shoude out to fight. Their men broke and fled back to the city.

sentences.zh: 貞大懼，閉閣自守。

translations.literal: Zhen was greatly afraid, shut his pavilion and guarded himself.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhen shut himself up in his quarters.

sentences.zh: 崇裕等至城下，左右謂貞曰：「王豈可坐待戮辱！」

translations.literal: Qu Chongyu and others reached below the city; attendants said to Zhen: "Your Highness — how can you sit waiting for slaughter and humiliation!
translations.idiomatic: When the government troops reached the walls, his attendants urged, "My lord, you cannot sit here waiting to be butchered and shamed!

sentences.zh: 貞、規、守德及其妻皆自殺。

translations.literal: Zhen, Gui, Shoude, and their wives all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, his son Gui, Pei Shoude, and their wives all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 與沖皆梟首東都闕下。

translations.literal: Together with Chong, their heads were hung at the eastern capital beneath the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Their heads were hung beside Chong's beneath the gate tower of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 初，范陽王藹遣使語貞及沖曰：「若四方諸王一時並起，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: Initially, Prince Ai of Fanyang sent envoys to tell Zhen and Chong: "If the princes of the four directions all rise at once, the affair cannot fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Ai of Fanyang had sent messengers to Zhen and Chong saying, "If all the princes rise together at once, we cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 諸王往來相約結，未定而沖先發，惟貞狼狽應之，諸王皆不敢發，故敗。

translations.literal: The princes passed back and forth making mutual covenants, but before it was settled Chong rose first — only Zhen responded in disarray; all the princes dared not rise, and therefore were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The princes had been exchanging pledges to revolt together, but before their plans were firm Chong struck first. Only Zhen answered in haste and confusion; the others never dared move, and that was why both rebellions collapsed.

sentences.zh: 貞之將起兵也，遣使告壽州刺史越環，環妻常樂公主謂使者曰：「為我語越王：昔隋文帝將篡周室，尉遲迥，周之甥也，猶能舉兵匡救社稷。

translations.literal: When Zhen was about to raise troops, he sent an envoy to notify Shouzhou Prefect Yue Huan; Huan's wife, the Princess of Changle, said to the envoy: "Speak for me to the Prince of Yue: In the past when Emperor Wen of Sui was about to usurp the Zhou house, Yuwen Jiong — Zhou's own nephew by marriage — could still raise troops to rescue and restore the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince Zhen prepared to rebel, he sent word to Yue Huan, prefect of Shouzhou. Huan's wife, the Princess of Changle, told the messenger, "Go tell the Prince of Yue: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to seize the Zhou throne, Yuwen Jiong — a nephew of the Zhou by marriage — still took up arms to defend the realm.

sentences.zh: 功雖不成，威震海內，足為忠烈。

translations.literal: Though the merit did not succeed, his majesty shook the inner seas — enough to count as a loyal and stalwart martyr.
translations.idiomatic: He did not succeed, yet his fame shook the empire and made him a model of loyal martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 況汝諸王，先帝之子，豈得不以社稷為心！

translations.literal: How much the more you princes — sons of the former emperor — how can you not take the altars of state to heart!
translations.idiomatic: You are sons of the late emperor — how can you fail to put the dynasty first!

sentences.zh: 今李氏危若朝露，汝諸王不捨生取義，尚猶豫不發，欲何須邪！

translations.literal: Now the Li clan is in peril like morning dew — you princes, not abandoning life to grasp righteousness, still hesitate and do not rise — what do you wait for!
translations.idiomatic: The Li house now hangs by a thread. If you princes will not risk your lives for what is right and still hang back, what are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 禍且至矣，大丈夫當為忠義鬼，無為徒死也。」

translations.literal: Calamity is about to arrive — a great man ought to become a ghost of loyalty and righteousness, not die in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is at hand. A true man should die a loyal martyr's death, not throw his life away for nothing."

sentences.zh: 及貞敗，太后欲悉誅韓、魯等諸王，命監察御史藍田蘇□按其密狀。

translations.literal: When Zhen was defeated, the Empress Dowager wished to execute entirely the Han, Lu, and other princes, and ordered Supervising Censor Lantian Su Xiong to investigate according to their secret denunciations.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's defeat, the Empress Dowager meant to put all the princes of Han, Lu, and the rest to death, and ordered Supervising Censor Su Xiong of Lantian to investigate the secret accusations against them.

sentences.zh: □訊問，皆無明驗，或告□與韓、魯通謀，太后召□詰之，□抗論不回。

translations.literal: Xiong examined and questioned — all had no clear proof; someone informed that Xiong was in conspiracy with Han and Lu — the Empress Dowager summoned Xiong to interrogate him; Xiong argued firmly and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong questioned the suspects but found no solid evidence. Someone then accused Xiong himself of plotting with the Han and Lu princes. The Empress Dowager summoned him for an accounting, but he stood his ground and would not budge.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿大雅之士，朕當別有任使，此獄不必卿也。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "You are a man of great refinement — I shall separately have other employment for you; this case need not involve you.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "You are a man of fine character. I shall find other work for you — this investigation is not yours to conduct.

sentences.zh: 乃命□於河西監軍，更使周興等按之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she ordered Xiong to supervise troops at Hexi, and changed to sending Zhou Xing and others to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent Xiong to oversee troops on the Hexi frontier and replaced him with Zhou Xing and others to continue the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 於是收韓王元喜、魯王靈夔、黃公譔、常樂公主於東都，迫脅皆自殺，更其姓曰「虺」，親黨皆誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Han Yuanxi, Prince Lingqi of Lu, Duke Zuan of Huang, and the Princess of Changle were seized at the Eastern Capital; coerced, all killed themselves; their surnames were changed to "Hui"; kinsmen and partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The court then seized Prince of Han Yuanxi, Prince Lingqi of Lu, Duke Zuan of Huang, and the Princess of Changle in the eastern capital. Under pressure, they all took their own lives. Their surname was changed to Hui, and their families and allies were put to death.

sentences.zh: 以文昌左丞狄仁傑為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Appointed Wenchang Left Assistant Di Renjie as Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie, left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, was made prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時治越王貞黨與，當坐者六七百家，籍沒者五千口，司刑趣使行刑。

translations.literal: At the time prosecuting Prince Zhen of Yue's associates — those due for punishment numbered six or seven hundred households; those whose property was confiscated, five thousand persons; the Minister of Punishments urged dispatch for carrying out executions.
translations.idiomatic: The courts were then punishing Prince Zhen's followers: six or seven hundred families faced execution, and five thousand people were slated for confiscation of property. The minister of punishments pressed to carry out the sentences at once.

sentences.zh: 仁傑密奏：「彼皆詿誤，臣欲顯奏，似為逆人申理；

translations.literal: Renjie secretly memorialized: "Those are all misled and implicated — I wish to openly memorialize, which seems like pleading the case for rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie sent a secret memorial: "These people were led astray. If I speak up openly, it will look as though I am defending rebels;

sentences.zh: 知而不言，恐乖陛下仁恤之旨。」

translations.literal: To know yet not speak — I fear it would contradict Your Majesty's benevolent and compassionate intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I know the truth and say nothing, I fear I will fail Your Majesty's merciful purpose.

sentences.zh: 太后特原之，皆流豐州。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager specially pardoned them — all were banished to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager specially spared them, and all were exiled to Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道過寧州，寧州父老迎勞之曰：「我狄使君活汝邪？」

translations.literal: Passing by Ningzhou, Ningzhou elders came to welcome and comfort them, saying: "Was it our Lord Di who gave you life?
translations.idiomatic: On the road they passed through Ning Prefecture, where the local elders came out to greet them, saying, "Was it Prefect Di who saved your lives?

sentences.zh: 相攜哭於德政碑下，設齋三日而後行。

translations.literal: Hand in hand they wept beneath the Monument of Virtuous Governance, set out vegetarian offerings for three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together at the Monument of Virtuous Governance, held three days of memorial offerings, and only then moved on.

sentences.zh: 時張光輔尚在豫州，將士恃功，多所求取，仁傑不之應。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Guangfu was still at Yuzhou — officers and soldiers relied on their merit and made many demands; Renjie did not respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangfu was still in Yuzhou, and his soldiers, flushed with victory, made endless demands. Renjie refused them.

sentences.zh: 光輔怒曰：「州將輕元帥邪？」

translations.literal: Guangfu angrily said: "Does the prefect belittle the commander-in-chief?
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu flew into a rage. "Does the prefect look down on the commander?

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「亂河南者，一越王貞耳，今一貞死，萬貞生！」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "The one who stirred chaos south of the Yellow River was only one Prince Zhen of Yue — now one Zhen dies, ten thousand Zhens are born!
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied, "Only one Prince of Yue brought turmoil to the region south of the Yellow River. Kill one Zhen, and you create ten thousand Zhens.

sentences.zh: 光輔詰其語，仁傑曰：「明公總兵三十萬，所誅者止於越王貞。

translations.literal: Guangfu interrogated the meaning of his words; Renjie said: "Your Excellency commands three hundred thousand troops — those executed reach only to Prince Zhen of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangfu pressed him to explain, Renjie said, "You command three hundred thousand men, yet the only rebel you needed to kill was Prince Zhen of Yue.

sentences.zh: 城中聞官軍至，逾城出降者四面成蹊，明公縱將士暴掠，殺已降以為功，流血丹野，非萬貞而何！

translations.literal: Within the cities, hearing the government army had arrived, those who climbed over walls to come out and surrender formed paths on all sides — Your Excellency indulges officers and soldiers in violent plunder, killing those already surrendered to make merit — blood flows reddening the fields: what is this if not ten thousand Zhens!
translations.idiomatic: When the city heard your army was coming, people poured out over the walls to surrender until the roads were crowded. Yet your men were allowed to loot freely and to butcher the surrendered for credit. The land ran red with blood — what is that if not breeding ten thousand Zhens?

sentences.zh: 恨不得尚方斬馬劍，加於明公之頸，雖死如歸耳！」

translations.literal: I only regret not having the Master of Works' horse-beheading sword to lay upon Your Excellency's neck — though I die, it would be like returning home!
translations.idiomatic: I only wish I had the imperial executioner's sword to put to your neck. I would gladly die for it.

sentences.zh: 光輔不能詰，歸，奏仁傑不遜，左遷復州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangfu could not interrogate further; on returning, memorialized that Renjie was insubordinate — demoted him to Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu had no answer. After he returned to court, he reported Renjie for insubordination, and Renjie was demoted to prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，左肅政大夫騫味道、夏官侍郎王本立並同平章事。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Left Censorate Grand Counselor Qian Weidao and Summer Office Vice Minister Wang Benli were both made co-equal chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, Left Censorate Grand Counselor Qian Weidao and Summer Office Vice Minister Wang Benli were both appointed co-equal chancellors.

sentences.zh: 太后之召宗室朝明堂也，東莞公融密遣使問成均助教高子貢，子貢曰：「來必死。」

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager summoned the imperial clan to court at the Bright Hall, Duke Rong of Dongguan secretly sent an envoy to ask Chengjun Assistant Instructor Gao Zigong; Zigong said: "Come and you will surely die.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager summoned the princes to attend at the Bright Hall, Duke Rong of Dongguan secretly sent to Gao Zigong, an assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy, to ask what awaited him. Zigong answered, "If you go, you will die.

sentences.zh: 融乃稱疾不赴。

translations.literal: Rong then claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Rong thereupon pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 越王貞起兵，遣使約融，融倉猝不能應，為官屬所逼，執使者以聞，擢拜右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen of Yue raised troops, sent an envoy to invite Rong; Rong could not respond in haste, was compelled by official subordinates, seized the envoy and reported it — was promoted and appointed Right Admonisher of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen of Yue rebelled, he sent a messenger to win Rong's support. Caught off guard, Rong was pressed by his staff to arrest the envoy and report the overture to the throne. He was rewarded with appointment as right admonisher of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為支黨所引，冬，十月，己亥，戮於市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Before long, he was implicated by associates; winter, tenth month, day jihai — executed in the market, household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was linked to the rebels by association. In the tenth month, on the jihai day, he was executed in public and his family property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 高子貢亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Gao Zigong also was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zigong was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史薛顗、顗弟緒、緒弟駙馬都尉紹，皆與琅邪王沖通謀。

translations.literal: Jizhou Prefect Xue Yan, Yan's younger brother Xu, and Xu's younger brother, Empress's Son-in-Law Commandant Shao — all were in communication and conspiracy with Prince Chong of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yan, prefect of Ji Prefecture, his younger brothers Xu and Shao the empress's son-in-law, had all been in secret contact with Prince Chong of Langye.

sentences.zh: 顗聞衝起兵，作兵器，募人；

translations.literal: Yan heard Chong had raised troops, made weapons, and recruited men;
translations.idiomatic: When Yan heard that Chong had revolted, he began forging weapons and recruiting troops;

sentences.zh: 沖敗，殺錄事參軍高纂以滅口。

translations.literal: When Chong was defeated, he killed Records-keeping Adjunct Gao Zuan to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's defeat, Yan killed his records officer Gao Zuan to silence him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛酉，顗、緒伏誅，紹以太平公主故，杖一百，餓死於獄。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day xinyou — Yan and Xu were executed by beheading; Shao, because of the Princess of Taiping, received a hundred strokes with the staff and starved to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the xinyou day, Yan and Xu were beheaded. Because Shao was the husband of the Princess of Taiping, he was given a hundred blows with the staff and left to starve in prison.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，司徒、青州刺史霍王元軌坐與越王連謀，廢徙黔州，載以檻車，行至陳倉而死。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yiyou — Minister of Education, Qingzhou Prefect Prince Yuan Gui of Huo, convicted of joining conspiracy with Prince of Yue, was deposed and banished to Qianzhou, carried in a caged cart — on reaching Chencang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the yiyou day, Prince Yuan Gui of Huo, minister of education and prefect of Qing, was found to have plotted with Prince Zhen of Yue. He was stripped of rank, exiled to Qian Prefecture in a barred cart, and died at Chencang on the way.

sentences.zh: 江都王緒、殿中監成公裴承先皆戮於市。

translations.literal: Prince Xu of Jiangdu, Director of the Palace Ateliers Duke Cheng Pei Chenxian — both were executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xu of Jiangdu and Director of the Palace Ateliers Duke Cheng Pei Chenxian were both executed in public.

sentences.zh: 承先，寂之孫也。

translations.literal: Chenxian was the grandson of Ji [Pei Ji].
translations.idiomatic: Chenxian was a grandson of Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 命裴居道留守西京。

translations.literal: Ordered Pei Judao to remain and guard the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Judao was ordered to remain as regent of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 左肅政大夫、同平章事騫味道素不禮於殿中侍御史周矩，屢言其不能了事。

translations.literal: Left Censorate Grand Counselor, Co-equal Chancellor Qian Weidao had always been discourteous to Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Censor Zhou Ju, repeatedly saying he could not finish affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weidao, left censorate grand counselor and co-equal chancellor, had long snubbed Palace Censor Zhou Ju and often mocked him as incompetent.

sentences.zh: 會有羅告味道者，敕矩按之。

translations.literal: It happened that someone spread accusations against Weidao; an edict ordered Ju to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: When someone denounced Weidao, the Empress Dowager ordered Ju to investigate.

sentences.zh: 矩謂味道曰：「公常責矩不了事，今日為公了之。」

translations.literal: Ju said to Weidao: "Your Excellency always reproaches Ju for not finishing affairs — today I finish them for Your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: Ju told Weidao, "You always said I couldn't finish a case. Today I've finished yours.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，味道及其子辭玉皆伏誅。

translations.literal: On day yihai, Weidao and his son Ciyu were both executed by beheading.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, Weidao and his son Ciyu were both beheaded.

sentences.zh: 己酉，太后拜洛受圖，皇帝、皇太子皆從，內外文武百官、蠻夷酋長各依方敘立，珍禽、奇獸、雜寶列於壇前，文物鹵簿之盛，唐興以來未之有也。

translations.literal: On day jiyou, the Empress Dowager performed the Lo River ceremony to receive the Mandate; the Emperor and Crown Prince both followed; inner and outer civil and military officials, chieftains of barbarians and Yi, each according to direction took their positions; rare birds, strange beasts, and miscellaneous treasures were arrayed before the altar — the splendor of cultural objects and ritual insignia had not been seen since Tang's rise.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day the Empress Dowager performed the rite of receiving the Heavenly Mandate at Luoyang. The emperor and crown prince attended, civil and military officials and foreign chieftains stood in their assigned ranks, and rare birds, exotic animals, and treasures were displayed before the altar. The pomp of ritual regalia surpassed anything since the founding of Tang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，明堂成，高二百九十四尺，方三百尺。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the Bright Hall was completed — height two hundred ninety-four feet, width three hundred feet square.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day the Bright Hall was finished: two hundred ninety-four feet high and three hundred feet square.

sentences.zh: 凡三層：下層法四時，各隨方色。

translations.literal: In all three tiers: the lower tier modeled on the four seasons, each following the color of its direction.
translations.idiomatic: It had three levels. The lowest followed the four seasons, each side painted in its seasonal color.

sentences.zh: 中層法十二辰；

translations.literal: The middle tier modeled on the twelve chronograms;
translations.idiomatic: The middle level represented the twelve earthly branches;

sentences.zh: 上為圓蓋，九龍捧之。

translations.literal: Above was a round canopy, nine dragons holding it up.
translations.idiomatic: At the top was a round cap held aloft by nine dragons.

sentences.zh: 上層法二十四氣；

translations.literal: The upper tier modeled on the twenty-four qi periods;
translations.idiomatic: The upper level symbolized the twenty-four solar terms;

sentences.zh: 亦為圓蓋，上施鐵鳳，高一丈，飾以黃金。

translations.literal: Also a round canopy; atop it was set an iron phoenix, height one zhang, decorated with gold.
translations.idiomatic: It too had a round cap, topped by an iron phoenix ten feet high, plated in gold.

sentences.zh: 中有巨木十圍，上下通貫，栭櫨棤藉以為本。

translations.literal: Within was a great tree ten arm-spans around, penetrating through top to bottom; bracket-sets and corbel blocks were piled as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: A trunk ten arm-spans thick ran straight through the structure, with bracket clusters layered as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 下施鐵渠，為辟雍之象。

translations.literal: Below was set an iron channel, in the likeness of a Pi-Yong.
translations.idiomatic: An iron moat at the base evoked the ceremonial Pi-Yong.

sentences.zh: 號曰萬象神宮。

translations.literal: It was titled the Palace of Myriad Images and Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: It was named the Palace of Myriad Forms and Spirits.

sentences.zh: 宴賜君臣，赦天下，縱民入觀。

translations.literal: Feasted and bestowed gifts on ruler and ministers, amnestied all under Heaven, allowed the people to enter and view.
translations.idiomatic: She feasted her ministers, proclaimed a general amnesty, and opened the hall to the public.

sentences.zh: 改河南為合宮縣。

translations.literal: Changed Henan to Hegong County.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture was renamed Hegong County.

sentences.zh: 又於明堂北起天堂五級以貯大像；

translations.literal: Further, north of the Bright Hall they raised the Heavenly Hall of five tiers to store the great image;
translations.idiomatic: North of the Bright Hall they also built the five-story Heavenly Hall to house the great Buddha image;

sentences.zh: 至三級，則俯視明堂矣。

translations.literal: Reaching the third tier, one could look down upon the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: From the third story one could look down on the Bright Hall itself.

sentences.zh: 僧懷義以功拜左威衛大將軍、梁國公。

translations.literal: The monk Huaiyi, for his merit, was appointed Left Weywei Grand General and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huaiyi was made Left Weywei Grand General and duke of Liang for his service.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王求禮上書曰：「古之明堂，茅茨不剪，采椽不斫。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Wang Qiuli memorialized: "The Bright Halls of antiquity used untrimmed thatch and undressed rafters.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Wang Qiuli submitted a memorial: "The Bright Halls of old were thatched and never trimmed, built with plain timber never dressed.

sentences.zh: 今者飾以珠玉，圖以丹青，鐵鷟入雲，金龍隱霧，昔殷辛瓊台，夏癸瑤室，無以加也。」

translations.literal: Now it is adorned with pearls and jade, painted with cinnabar and green; iron owls enter the clouds, golden dragons hidden in mist — in the past King Xin of Yin's Jade Terrace and King Gui of Xia's Jasper Chamber could add nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Yours is studded with pearls and jade, painted in red and green, with iron owls piercing the clouds and gold dragons lost in mist. The Jade Terrace of King Zhou of Shang and the Jasper Chamber of King Jie of Xia had nothing on it.

sentences.zh: 太后不報。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager did not respond.

sentences.zh: 太后欲發梁、鳳、巴蜑，自雅州開山能道，出擊生羌，因襲吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to mobilize the Liang, Feng, and Ba Dan peoples, from Yazhou open a mountain route, issue forth to strike the Raw Qiang, and thereby raid Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager planned to levy troops from the Liang, Feng, and Ba Dan peoples, cut a road through the mountains from Ya Prefecture, attack the Raw Qiang, and strike Tibet from there.

sentences.zh: 正字陳子昂上書，以為：「雅州邊羌，自國初以來未嘗為盜。

translations.literal: Rectifier Chen Zi'ang memorialized, holding: "The border Qiang of Yazhou, since the founding of the state, have never been bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifier Chen Zi'ang submitted a memorial arguing that the frontier Qiang near Ya Prefecture had never raided the borders since the dynasty was founded.

sentences.zh: 今一旦無罪戮之，其怨必甚；

translations.literal: Now at once, without guilt, to slaughter them — their resentment will surely be extreme;
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter them without cause now, and their hatred will be bitter;

sentences.zh: 且懼誅滅，必蜂起為盜。

translations.literal: Moreover, fearing extermination, they will surely swarm up as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing extermination, they will surely rise in rebellion like hornets.

sentences.zh: 西山盜起，則蜀之邊邑不得不連兵備守，兵久不解，臣愚以為西蜀之禍，自此結矣。

translations.literal: If bandits rise in the western mountains, then Shu's border settlements cannot but link forces to guard and defend; troops long not dismissed — your subject in his foolishness considers that western Shu's calamity is thereby knotted from this.
translations.idiomatic: If banditry flares in the western hills, every border post in Shu will have to keep troops under arms. A war that never ends — I believe the disaster for western Shu will begin here.

sentences.zh: 臣聞吐蕃愛蜀富饒，欲盜之久矣，徒以山川阻絕，障隘不通，勢不能動。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Tubo loves Shu's wealth and abundance, has long wished to plunder it — only because mountains and rivers block and cut off, barrier passes do not connect, the situation cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Tibet covets the riches of Shu and has long wanted to seize them, but rugged terrain and closed passes have kept it from moving.

sentences.zh: 今國家乃亂邊羌，開隘道，使其收奔亡之種，為鄉導以攻邊，是借寇兵而為賊除道，舉全蜀以遺之也。

translations.literal: Now the state stirs up the border Qiang, opens pass routes, enabling them to gather fleeing exiled tribes, act as local guides to attack the borders — this is lending bandit troops and clearing the road for thieves, presenting all of Shu to give away.
translations.idiomatic: To stir up the frontier Qiang, open mountain passes, and let fleeing tribes rally as guides against our own borders is to lend the enemy soldiers and blaze a trail for invaders — it is to hand all of Shu over as a gift.

sentences.zh: 蜀者國家之寶庫，可以兼濟中國。

translations.literal: Shu is the state's treasure vault, able to support and relieve the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is the empire's storehouse, the region that feeds the heartland.

sentences.zh: 今執事者乃圖僥倖之利以事西羌，得其地不足以稼穡，財不足以富國，徒為糜費，無益聖德，況其成敗未可知哉！

translations.literal: Now those in charge only plot lucky windfall profit to engage the western Qiang — obtain their land, not enough for planting and harvest; wealth, not enough to enrich the state — merely wasted expenditure, no benefit to sagely virtue; moreover, its success or failure cannot yet be known!
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge now chase a gambler's profit against the western Qiang. The land won will not feed armies, the treasure won will not enrich the state. It is waste without honor — and the outcome is far from certain.

sentences.zh: 夫蜀之所恃者險也，人之所以安者無役也；

translations.literal: What Shu relies upon is its perilous terrain; what its people rely on for peace is freedom from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Shu rests on its natural defenses; its people rest on freedom from forced labor;

sentences.zh: 今國家乃開其險，役其人，險開則便寇，人役則傷財，臣恐未見羌戎，已有奸盜在其中矣。

translations.literal: Now the state opens its peril, drafts its people — peril opened then bandits are facilitated; people drafted then wealth is harmed — your subject fears that before even seeing Qiang and Rong, there will already be traitors and bandits within.
translations.idiomatic: Open the passes and you ease the enemy's road; draft the people and you drain the treasury. I fear that before we even meet the Qiang, bandits will already be at work within Shu.

sentences.zh: 且蜀人尪劣，不習兵戰，山川阻曠，去中夏遠，今無故生西羌、吐蕃之患，臣見其不及百年，蜀為戎矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Shu people are weak and inferior, unaccustomed to military warfare; mountains and rivers are vast and remote, far from the Central Xia — now without cause producing the calamity of western Qiang and Tubo — your subject sees that within less than a century, Shu will become Rong territory.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu are frail and untrained in war. Their land is vast and remote from the heartland. Provoke Tibet and the Qiang without cause, and I see Shu becoming foreign territory within a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 國家近廢安北，拔單于，棄龜茲，放疏勒，天下翕然謂之盛德者，蓋以陛下務在養人，不在廣地也。

translations.literal: The state recently abolished the Protectorate of the Peaceful North, withdrew from Chanyu, abandoned Kucha, released Kashgar — all under Heaven unanimously called this sagely virtue, because Your Majesty's task lay in nurturing people, not in expanding territory.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lately withdrawn from the north — abolishing the Protectorate of the Peaceful North, abandoning Chanyu, giving up Kucha and Kashgar — and the empire praised this as great virtue because you sought to nurture people, not to seize land.

sentences.zh: 今山東饑，關、隴弊，而徇貪夫之議，謀動甲兵，興大役，自古國亡家敗，未嘗不由黷兵，願陛下熟計之。」

translations.literal: Now Shandong is famine-stricken, Guan and Long are exhausted — yet to follow greedy men's counsel, plot to move armor and troops, raise great corvée — since antiquity, states perished and families ruined, never not from licentious warfare — Your Majesty, I wish you would carefully calculate this.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong is starving and the northwest is exhausted. To heed greedy counsels, mobilize armies, and launch grand public works — dynasties have fallen before from just such rash wars. I beg Your Majesty to weigh this with care.

sentences.zh: 既而役不果興。

translations.literal: In the end the corvée project was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the campaign was never launched.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯朔，大饗萬象神宮，太后服袞冕，搢大圭，執鎮圭為初獻，皇帝為亞獻，太子為終獻。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day yimao on the new moon, a grand offering was performed at the Palace of Myriad Forms; the Empress Dowager wore sacrificial robes and dragon crown, inserted the great jade tablet, and held the territorial jade tablet for the first offering; the Emperor made the second offering; the Crown Prince made the final offering.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the yimao day, a great sacrifice was held at the Palace of Myriad Forms. The Empress Dowager wore full ceremonial dress, presented the great jade tablet, and performed the first offering with the territorial tablet; the emperor performed the second offering, and the crown prince the third.

sentences.zh: 先詣昊天上帝座，次高祖、太宗、高宗，次魏國先王，次五方帝座。

translations.literal: First they proceeded to the seat of August Heaven, then to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, then to the former kings of Wei, then to the seats of the Five Directional Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: They first approached the throne of August Heaven, then those of Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, then the ancestral kings of Wei, and finally the thrones of the Five Directional Emperors.

sentences.zh: 太后御則天門，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager held court at the Zetian Gate, amnestied all under Heaven, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager took her seat at the Zetian Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，太后御明堂，受朝賀。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, the Empress Dowager held the Bright Hall and received court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day the Empress Dowager entered the Bright Hall and received the court's homage.

sentences.zh: 戊午，布政於明堂，頒九條以訓百官。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, she announced governance at the Bright Hall and issued the Nine Articles to instruct the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day she proclaimed her policies in the Bright Hall and promulgated the Nine Articles as instruction for the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 己未，御明堂，饗群臣。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, she held the Bright Hall and feasted the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day she again entered the Bright Hall and entertained the officials.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁酉，尊魏忠孝王曰周忠孝太皇，妣曰忠孝太后，文水陵曰章德陵，咸陽陵曰明義陵。

translations.literal: Second month, day dingyou, the Wei Loyal and Filial King was honored as Zhou Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; his mother was honored as Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager; the Wenshui tomb was named the Zhangde Tomb, and the Xianyang tomb the Mingyi Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the dingyou day, Wu Zetian's father was posthumously honored as Grand Emperor Loyal and Filial of Zhou, his consort as Empress Dowager Loyal and Filial, the Wenshui tomb renamed Zhangde, and the Xianyang tomb Mingyi.

sentences.zh: 置崇先府官。

translations.literal: Officials of the Glorify-Ancestors Prefecture were established.
translations.idiomatic: An office was created to oversee the Glorify-Ancestors Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，尊魯公曰太原靖王，北平王曰趙肅恭王，金城王曰魏義康王，太原王曰周安成王。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, the Duke of Lu was honored as Prince Jing of Taiyuan, the Prince of Beiping as Prince Su and Gong of Zhao, the Prince of Jincheng as Prince Yi and Kang of Wei, and the Prince of Taiyuan as Prince An and Cheng of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day her ancestors were further ennobled: the Duke of Lu as Prince Jing of Taiyuan, the Prince of Beiping as Prince Su and Gong of Zhao, the Prince of Jincheng as Prince Yi and Kang of Wei, and the Prince of Taiyuan as Prince An and Cheng of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲子，張光輔守納言。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi, Zhang Guangfu served as acting Speaker.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiazi day, Zhang Guangfu was appointed acting Speaker of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬申，太后問正字陳子昂當今為政之要。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the Empress Dowager asked Rectifier Chen Zi'ang about the essentials of governing the present age.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day the Empress Dowager asked Chen Zi'ang, a rectifier in the Palace Library, what mattered most in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 子昂退，上疏，以為：「宜緩刑崇德，息兵革，省賦役，撫慰宗室，各使自安。」

translations.literal: Zi'ang withdrew and submitted a memorial, holding: "One should ease punishments and honor virtue, cease arms and armor, reduce taxes and corvée, and comfort the imperial clan so that each may find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang withdrew and memorialized the throne, arguing that she should lighten punishments and exalt virtue, halt warfare, cut taxes and forced labor, and reassure the imperial clan so that each branch might live in peace.

sentences.zh: 辭婉意切，其論甚美，幾三千言。

translations.literal: The words were refined and the intent earnest; the argument was very fine, nearly three thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: His language was graceful and his counsel urgent; the essay was nearly three thousand characters long and altogether admirable.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以天官尚書武承嗣為納言，張光輔守內史。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, Heavenly Office Minister Wu Chengsi was made Speaker, and Zhang Guangfu served as acting Inner Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Wu Chengsi was appointed Speaker, and Zhang Guangfu became acting Inner Administrator.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，殺辰州別駕汝南王煒、連州別駕鄱陽公諲等宗室十二人，徙其家於巂州。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiachen, twelve members of the imperial clan were killed, including Runan Prince Wei, Chen Prefecture vice prefect, and Poyang Duke Shen, Lian Prefecture vice prefect; their families were relocated to Xi Prefecture.
