translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the jiachen day, twelve imperial clansmen were executed, among them Runan Prince Wei, vice prefect of Chen Prefecture, and Poyang Duke Shen, vice prefect of Lian Prefecture; their households were banished to Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 煒，惲之子；

translations.literal: Wei was the son of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was a son of Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 諲，元慶之子也。

translations.literal: Shen was the son of Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was a son of Li Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 己酉，殺天官侍郎藍田鄧玄挺。

translations.literal: On day jiyou, Heavenly Office Vice Minister Deng Xuanting of Lantian was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day Deng Xuanting of Lantian, vice minister of the Heavenly Office, was executed.

sentences.zh: 玄挺女為諲妻，又與煒善。

translations.literal: Xuanting's daughter was Shen's wife, and he was also on good terms with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanting's daughter was married to Shen, and he was also close to Wei.

sentences.zh: 諲謀迎中宗於廬陵，以問玄挺，煒又嘗謂玄挺曰：「欲為急計，何如？」

translations.literal: Shen plotted to welcome Zhongzong from Luling and asked Xuanting about it; Wei also once said to Xuanting: "If one wishes to take urgent measures, what would you think?
translations.idiomatic: Shen plotted to bring Emperor Zhongzong back from exile in Luling and consulted Xuanting; Wei too had once asked him, "If we mean to act at once, what do you say?

sentences.zh: 玄挺皆不應。

translations.literal: Xuanting did not respond to either.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanting answered neither man.

sentences.zh: 故坐知反不告，同誅。

translations.literal: Therefore he was punished for knowing of rebellion and not reporting it, and was executed together with them.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore condemned for knowing of treason and failing to report it, and was put to death with the rest.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙辰，命文昌右相韋待價為安息道行軍大總管，擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingchen, Literary Glory Right Chancellor Wei Daibao was appointed Grand Commander of the Anxi Circuit campaign army to strike Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingchen day, Wei Daibao, right chancellor of Literary Glory, was made grand campaign commander of the Anxi Circuit to attack Tibet.

sentences.zh: 浪穹州蠻酋傍時昔等二十五部，先附吐蕃，至是來降；

translations.literal: Twenty-five tribal divisions under the Langqiong chieftain Bangshixi and others, who had formerly submitted to Tubo, now came to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five tribal groups under Bangshixi, chieftain of Langqiong, who had previously sided with Tibet, now submitted;

sentences.zh: 以傍時昔為浪穹州刺史，令統其眾。

translations.literal: Bangshixi was made governor of Langqiong Prefecture and ordered to command his people.
translations.idiomatic: Bangshixi was appointed governor of Langqiong and placed in command of his followers.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以僧懷義為新平軍大總管，北討突厥。

translations.literal: On day jisi, the monk Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Xiping Army to campaign north against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day the monk Huaiyi was appointed grand commander of the Xiping Army and sent north against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 行至紫河，不見虜，於單于台刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Zi River it saw no enemy; at the Chanyu Platform it carved stone to record merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched as far as the Zi River without finding the enemy, carved a stone monument to its achievement on the Chanyu Platform, and came home.

sentences.zh: 諸王之起兵也，貝州刺史紀王慎獨不預謀，亦坐繫獄；

translations.literal: When the princes raised troops, Prince Ji Shen of Bei Prefecture alone had not joined the plot, yet he too was imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: When the princes took up arms, Prince Ji Shen, governor of Bei Prefecture, had taken no part in the conspiracy, yet he too was thrown into prison;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，檻車徙巴州，更姓虺氏，行及蒲州而卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingsi, he was transported in a cage cart to Ba Prefecture, his surname changed to the Hui clan; en route at Pu Prefecture he died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the dingsi day he was sent in a cage cart to Ba Prefecture and forced to take the surname Hui; he died on the road at Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八男徐州刺史東平王續等，相繼被誅，家徙嶺南。

translations.literal: His eight sons, including Xu Prefecture governor Prince Xu of Dongping, were executed one after another, and their households were relocated to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His eight sons, among them Prince Xu of Dongping, governor of Xu Prefecture, were executed in turn, and their families were exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 女東光縣主楚媛，幼以孝謹稱，適司議郎裴仲將，相敬如賓；

translations.literal: His daughter, Commandery Lady Chuyuan of Dongguang, was known from youth for filial piety and careful conduct; she married Secretariat Discussion Officer Pei Zhongjiang, and they treated each other with the respect due to guests;
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Chuyuan, commandery lady of Dongguang, was famed from childhood for filial devotion and modesty. Married to Pei Zhongjiang, a secretariat discussion officer, the couple treated each other with the courtesy of honored guests;

sentences.zh: 姑有疾，親嘗藥膳；

translations.literal: when her mother-in-law fell ill, she personally tasted medicines and food;
translations.idiomatic: when her mother-in-law was ill she tasted every medicine and dish herself;

sentences.zh: 接遇娣姒，皆得歡心。

translations.literal: in receiving and treating her sisters-in-law, she won the hearts of all.
translations.idiomatic: and in her dealings with her sisters-in-law she won every heart in the household.

sentences.zh: 時宗室諸女皆以驕奢相尚，誚楚媛獨儉素，曰：「所貴於富貴者，得適志也；

translations.literal: At the time the daughters of the imperial clan all prized one another's arrogance and luxury, and mocked Chuyuan alone for plain living, saying: "What is prized in wealth and nobility is fulfilling one's will;
translations.idiomatic: The women of the imperial clan vied in pride and extravagance, and they mocked Chuyuan for living simply. "The whole point of rank and riches," they said, "is to do as one pleases;

sentences.zh: 今獨守勤苦，將以何求？」

translations.literal: now you alone keep to diligence and hardship — what do you seek?
translations.idiomatic: yet you alone cling to toil and hardship. What are you after?

sentences.zh: 楚媛曰：「幼而好禮，今而行之，非適志歟！

translations.literal: Chuyuan said: "From youth I loved ritual — now I practice it; is this not fulfilling one's will!
translations.idiomatic: Chuyuan replied, "I have loved propriety since I was a child, and now I live by it. Is that not doing as I please?

sentences.zh: 觀自古女子，皆以恭儉為美，縱侈為惡。

translations.literal: Looking at women since antiquity, all have taken respectful frugality as beautiful and unrestrained extravagance as evil.
translations.idiomatic: Look at women through the ages: respectful thrift is held beautiful, wanton luxury is held shameful.

sentences.zh: 辱親是懼，何所求乎；

translations.literal: I fear shaming my kin — what is there to seek?
translations.idiomatic: I fear only disgracing my family. What else could I want?

sentences.zh: 富貴倘來之物，何足驕人！」

translations.literal: Wealth and nobility are things that may come by chance — what worth is there in being arrogant toward others!
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and rank are gifts that may vanish overnight. What pride is there in them?

sentences.zh: 眾皆慚服。

translations.literal: All were ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The others were abashed and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及慎凶問至，楚媛號慟，嘔血數升；

translations.literal: When news of Shen's death arrived, Chuyuan wailed in grief and vomited several sheng of blood;
translations.idiomatic: When word came of Shen's death, Chuyuan wailed until she vomited blood by the quart;

sentences.zh: 免喪，不御膏沐者垂二十年。

translations.literal: after the mourning period ended, for nearly twenty years she did not use ointments or wash her hair.
translations.idiomatic: and for nearly twenty years after mourning ended she refused oils and bathing.

sentences.zh: 韋待價軍至寅識迦河，與吐蕃戰，大敗。

translations.literal: Wei Daibao's army reached the Yinshijia River, fought Tubo, and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Daibao's army reached the Yinshijia River, met the Tibetans in battle, and was routed.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，糧運不繼。

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell, and grain transport could not continue.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow cut off the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 待價既無將領之才，狼狽失據，士卒凍餒，死亡甚眾，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Daibao lacked the talent of a commander; in disarray he lost his footing, soldiers froze and starved, and very many died; thereupon he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Daibao proved no general. His force fell apart, men froze and starved, casualties mounted, and he retreated.

sentences.zh: 太后大怒，丙子，待價除名，流繡州，斬副大總管安西大都護閻溫古。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was greatly angered; on day bingzi, Daibao was stripped of his name and exiled to Xiuzhou, and Deputy Grand Commander Yan Wengu, Protector-General of Anxi, was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was furious. On the bingzi day Daibao was stripped of rank and banished to Xiuzhou, and Yan Wengu, deputy commander and protector-general of Anxi, was executed.

sentences.zh: 安西副都護唐休璟收其餘眾，撫安西土，太后以休璟為西州都督。

translations.literal: Anxi Vice Protector Tang Xiujing gathered the remaining troops and pacified the Western Regions; the Empress Dowager made Xiujing governor of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xiujing, vice protector of Anxi, rallied the survivors and restored order in the west; the Empress Dowager appointed him governor of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以王本立同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Wang Benli was made co-equal with Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Wang Benli was appointed a third-rank co-equal with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業之敗也，弟敬真流繡州，逃歸，將奔突厥，過洛陽，洛州司馬弓嗣業、洛陽令張嗣明資遣之；

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye was defeated, his younger brother Jingzhen, exiled to Xiuzhou, escaped and returned, intending to flee to the Turks; passing through Luoyang, Lu Prefecture marshal Gong Siye and Luoyang magistrate Zhang Siming supplied and sent him on his way;
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Jingye's defeat his brother Jingzhen, banished to Xiuzhou, escaped and headed for the Turks. Passing through Luoyang, Lu Prefecture marshal Gong Siye and Luoyang magistrate Zhang Siming gave him money and sent him on;

sentences.zh: 至定州，為吏所獲，嗣業縊死。

translations.literal: When he reached Ding Prefecture he was seized by officials, and Siye hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Ding Prefecture he was captured by the authorities, and Siye hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 嗣明、敬真多引海內知識，雲有異圖，冀以免死；

translations.literal: Siming and Jingzhen implicated many acquaintances throughout the realm, claiming they had secret designs, hoping thereby to avoid death;
translations.idiomatic: Siming and Jingzhen implicated scores of acquaintances across the empire, alleging conspiracies in the hope of saving their own lives;

sentences.zh: 於是朝野之士為所連引坐死者甚眾。

translations.literal: thereupon very many court and countryside men were implicated by them and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: and a great many officials and private citizens died by implication.

sentences.zh: 嗣明誣內史張光輔，云「征豫州日，私論圖讖、天文，陰懷兩端。」

translations.literal: Siming falsely accused Inner Administrator Zhang Guangfu, saying: "On the day of campaigning against Yuzhou, he privately discussed prognostic charts and astronomy and secretly harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Siming falsely accused Inner Administrator Zhang Guangfu, declaring that during the campaign against Yuzhou he had privately discussed omens and astronomy and secretly wavered in his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲申，光輔與敬真、嗣明等同誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiashen, Guangfu was executed together with Jingzhen, Siming, and the rest, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the jiashen day, Guangfu was executed along with Jingzhen, Siming, and the others, and their property was seized.

sentences.zh: 乙未，秋官尚書太原張楚金、陝州刺史郭正一、鳳閣侍郎元萬頃、洛陽令魏元忠，並免死流嶺南。

translations.literal: On day yiwei, Autumn Office Minister Zhang Chujin of Taiyuan, Shaan Prefecture governor Guo Zhengyi, Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Yuan Wanqing, and Luoyang magistrate Wei Yuanzhong were all spared death and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day Zhang Chujin of Taiyuan, minister of the Autumn Office; Guo Zhengyi, governor of Shaan Prefecture; Yuan Wanqing, vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion; and Wei Yuanzhong, magistrate of Luoyang, were all spared execution and banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 楚金等皆為敬直所引，雲與敬業通謀。

translations.literal: Chujin and the others were all implicated by Jingzhen, who claimed they had conspired with Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Each had been named by Jingzhen as a co-conspirator of Jingye.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，太后使鳳閣舍人王隱客馳騎傳聲赦之。

translations.literal: As execution approached, the Empress Dowager sent Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Wang Yinku galloping on horseback to transmit by voice an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: At the scaffold the Empress Dowager sent Wang Yinku, an attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, galloping with a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 聲達於市，當刑者皆喜躍歡呼，宛轉不已；

translations.literal: The voice reached the market; those facing execution all leaped for joy and cried out, writhing without end;
translations.idiomatic: When the shout reached the marketplace the condemned leapt and cheered, weeping and shouting without pause;

sentences.zh: 元忠獨安坐自如，或使之起，元忠曰：「虛實未知。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong alone sat calmly as before; when someone told him to rise, Yuanzhong said: "Whether it is true or false is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: only Yuanzhong remained seated as calmly as before. When told to rise he said, "We do not yet know whether this is real.

sentences.zh: 隱客至，又使起，元忠曰：「俟宣敕已。」

translations.literal: When Yinku arrived and again told him to rise, Yuanzhong said: "Wait until the edict has been proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinku arrived and again bade him stand, Yuanzhong said, "Wait until the edict is read in full.

sentences.zh: 既宣敕，乃徐起，舞蹈再拜，竟無憂喜之色。

translations.literal: After the edict was proclaimed, he then slowly rose, performed the dance and bowed twice, and to the end showed no color of worry or joy.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the proclamation did he rise slowly, perform the ritual bow, and show neither relief nor exultation.

sentences.zh: 是日，陰雲四塞，既釋楚金等，天氣晴霽。

translations.literal: That day dark clouds blocked all four sides; once Chujin and the others were released, the weather cleared.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky had been overcast on every side; once Chujin and the others were freed, it broke into clear weather.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬子，以僧懷義為新平道行軍大總管，將兵二十萬以討突厥骨篤祿。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renzi, the monk Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Xiping Circuit campaign army, leading two hundred thousand troops to attack the Turk Gulou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renzi day, the monk Huaiyi was appointed grand campaign commander of the Xiping Circuit with two hundred thousand men to subdue the Turk Gulou.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗之世，周興以河陽令召見，上欲加擢用，或奏以非清流，罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Gaozong's reign, Zhou Xing was summoned for audience from his post as magistrate of Heyang; the emperor wished to promote and employ him further, but someone memorialized that he was not of clear-stream pedigree, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's day Zhou Xing had been summoned from his magistracy at Heyang for an audience. The emperor meant to promote him, but a memorial argued that he was not of reputable birth, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 興不知，數於明堂俟命。

translations.literal: Xing did not know this and repeatedly waited at the Bright Hall for orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xing knew nothing of this and kept waiting at the Bright Hall for his summons.

sentences.zh: 諸相皆無言，地官尚書、檢校納言魏玄同，時同平章事，謂之曰：「周明府可去矣。」

translations.literal: All the chancellors were silent; Earth Office Minister and acting Speaker Wei Xuantong, then co-equal with chancellors, said to him: "Magistrate Zhou may leave now.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors said nothing. Wei Xuantong, minister of the Earth Office, acting Speaker, and co-equal chancellor, finally told him, "Magistrate Zhou, you may go home.

sentences.zh: 興以為玄同沮己，銜之。

translations.literal: Xing thought Xuantong had obstructed him and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xing took this as deliberate obstruction and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 玄同素與裴炎善，時人以其終始不渝，謂之耐久朋。

translations.literal: Xuantong had long been on good terms with Pei Yan; people of the time, for his constancy from beginning to end, called him a durable friend.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong had long been close to Pei Yan, and contemporaries, admiring his constancy, called him a friend who endures.

sentences.zh: 周興奏誣玄同言：「太后老矣，不若奉嗣君為耐久。」

translations.literal: Zhou Xing memorialized falsely accusing Xuantong of saying: "The Empress Dowager is old; better to follow the heir as something durable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing then falsely reported that Xuantong had said, "The Empress Dowager is old. Better to cleave to the heir — that is the friendship that lasts.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，閏月，甲午，賜死於家。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angered; in the intercalary month, day jiawu, he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was enraged. In the intercalary month, on the jiawu day, he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 監刑御史房濟謂玄同曰：「丈人何不告密，冀得召見，可以自直！」

translations.literal: Supervising censor Fang Ji said to Xuantong: "Elder, why not inform in secret, hoping to be summoned for audience and clear yourself!
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor Fang Ji urged him, "Sir, why not inform on others? You might be summoned and clear your name!

sentences.zh: 玄同歎曰：「人殺鬼殺，亦復何殊，豈能作告密人邪！」

translations.literal: Xuantong sighed and said: "To be killed by men or killed by ghosts — what difference is there? How could I become an informer!
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong sighed. "Death at men's hands or death at ghosts' — what is the difference? How could I become an informer!

sentences.zh: 乃就死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted death.
translations.idiomatic: And he went to his death.

sentences.zh: 又殺夏官侍郎崔察於隱處。

translations.literal: Summer Office Vice Minister Cui Cha was also killed in a hidden place.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Office Vice Minister Cui Cha was also executed in secret.

sentences.zh: 自餘內外大臣坐死及流貶甚眾。

translations.literal: Of the rest, very many inner and outer great ministers were put to death or exiled and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Many other ministers within and without the court were executed or banished besides.

sentences.zh: 彭州長史劉易從亦為徐敬真所引；

translations.literal: Peng Prefecture chief assistant Liu Yicong was also implicated by Xu Jingzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yicong, chief assistant of Peng Prefecture, was also named by Xu Jingzhen;

sentences.zh: 戊申，就州誅之。

translations.literal: On day wushen, he was executed in his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and on the wushen day he was executed in his own province.

sentences.zh: 易從為人，仁孝忠謹，將刑於市，吏民憐其無辜，遠近奔赴，競解衣投地曰：「為長史求冥福。」

translations.literal: Yicong as a man was benevolent, filial, loyal, and careful; about to be executed in the market, officials and people pitied his innocence; from near and far they rushed to come, competing to remove their clothes and cast them on the ground, saying: "Seek afterlife blessing for the chief assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Yicong was known for kindness, filial piety, loyalty, and restraint. As he was led to the marketplace, officials and commoners alike mourned his innocence. People came from far and near, stripping off garments and casting them on the ground, crying, "We offer this for the chief assistant's peace in the next world.

sentences.zh: 有司平准，直十餘萬。

translations.literal: The authorities assessed them at standard value — worth more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities appraised the gifts at more than one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 周興等誣右武衛大將軍燕公黑齒常之謀反，征下獄。

translations.literal: Zhou Xing and others falsely accused Right Martial Guard Grand General Duke of Yan Heichi Changzhi of plotting rebellion; he was summoned and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing and his allies falsely accused Heichi Changzhi, grand general of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Yan, of treason; he was summoned and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊午，常之縊死。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuwu, Changzhi hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the wuwu day, Changzhi hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 己未，殺宗室鄂州剌史嗣鄭王璥等六人。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, six members of the imperial clan were killed, including E Prefecture governor Prince Jin of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day six imperial clansmen were executed, among them Prince Jin of Zheng, governor of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚申，嗣滕王修琦等六人免死，流嶺南。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, six men including Prince Xiu of Teng were spared death and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day six others, including Prince Xiu of Teng, were spared execution and banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，春官尚書范履冰、鳳閣侍郎邢文偉並同平章事。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Spring Office Minister Fan Lubing and Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Xing Wenwei were both made co-equal with chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Fan Lubing, minister of the Spring Office, and Xing Wenwei, vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, were both appointed co-equal chancellors.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔太穆神皇后、文德聖皇后宜配皇地示氏，忠孝太后從配。

translations.literal: On day jimao, an edict declared that Empress Taizu Shen and Empress Wende the Sage should be paired with the Earth Spirit, with Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager as secondary pairing.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day an edict ordered Empress Taizu Shen and Empress Wende the Sage paired in sacrifice with the Earth Spirit, with the Loyal and Filial Empress Dowager accorded secondary place.

sentences.zh: 右衛冑曹參軍陳子昂上疏，以為：「周頌成、康，漢稱文、景，皆以能措刑故也。

translations.literal: Right Guard Armor Bureau Officer Chen Zi'ang submitted a memorial, holding: "Zhou praised Cheng and Kang; Han praised Wen and Jing — all because they were able to set aside punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, an officer of the Right Guard armor bureau, memorialized the throne: "The Zhou praised King Cheng and King Kang; the Han praised Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing — all because they knew when to stay the hand of punishment.

sentences.zh: 今陛下之政，雖盡善矣，然太平之朝，上下樂化，不宜有亂臣賊子，日犯天誅。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's governance today, though wholly good, yet in an age of great peace, above and below rejoicing in transformation, there should not be traitors and wicked sons daily offending Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Your rule is already excellent, yet in a peaceful age, when court and country rejoice in your transforming influence, traitors ought not to be falling to the executioner's blade day after day.

sentences.zh: 比者大獄增多，逆徒滋廣，愚臣頑昧，初謂皆實，乃去月十五日，陛下特察系囚李珍等無罪，百僚慶悅，皆賀聖明，臣乃知亦有無罪之人掛於疏網者。

translations.literal: Recently great cases have increased and rebels proliferated; your foolish subject, dull and obscure, at first thought all were real. Yet on the fifteenth of last month Your Majesty specially examined prisoners Li Zhen and others and found them innocent; the hundred officials rejoiced and all congratulated your sagely clarity — then your subject knew that there are also innocent men caught in a loose net.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the great prosecutions have multiplied and the roll of 'rebels' grown ever longer. I, dull as I am, at first believed every charge. Then on the fifteenth of last month Your Majesty personally reviewed the cases of Li Zhen and others and found them innocent. The whole court rejoiced and praised your wisdom — and I realized that innocent men can indeed be snared in a slack net.

sentences.zh: 陛下務在寬典，獄官務在急刑，以傷陛下之仁，以誣太平之政，臣竊恨之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty strives for lenient law, yet prison officials strive for hasty punishment — this harms Your Majesty's benevolence and slanders the governance of great peace; your subject privately resents this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks clemency, yet the prison officials rush toward harsh sentences. This wounds your benevolence and makes a mockery of an age of peace. I cannot but grieve over it.

sentences.zh: 又，九月二十一日敕免楚金等死，初有風雨，變為景雲。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the twenty-first day of the ninth month an edict spared Chujin and the others from death; at first there was wind and rain, which changed into bright clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when the edict of the twenty-first of the ninth month spared Chujin and the others, storm clouds at first gave way to bright sky.

sentences.zh: 臣聞陰慘者刑也，陽舒者德也；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that yin gloom is punishment and yang ease is virtue;
translations.idiomatic: I have read that gloom belongs to punishment and clear weather to virtue;

sentences.zh: 聖人法天，天亦助聖。

translations.literal: the sage takes Heaven as model, and Heaven also aids the sage.
translations.idiomatic: the sage takes Heaven as his model, and Heaven in turn aids the sage.

sentences.zh: 天意如此，陛下豈可不承順之哉！

translations.literal: Heaven's intent is thus — how can Your Majesty not follow and accord with it!
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven speaks so plainly, how can Your Majesty fail to heed it!

sentences.zh: 今又陰雨，臣恐過在獄官。

translations.literal: Now again there is overcast rain; your subject fears the fault lies with the prison officials.
translations.idiomatic: Now the skies are dark again, and I fear the fault lies with the prison officials.

sentences.zh: 凡繫獄之囚，多在極法，道路之議，或是或非，陛下何不悉召見之，自詰其罪。

translations.literal: In general, prisoners in custody mostly face the extreme penalty; public talk on the roads is uncertain, right or wrong — why does Your Majesty not summon them all for audience and personally interrogate their crimes?
translations.idiomatic: Most of those in custody face the death penalty, and rumor in the streets cannot tell guilt from innocence. Why not summon every prisoner before you and question each case yourself?

sentences.zh: 罪有實者顯示明刑，濫者嚴懲獄吏，使天下鹹服，人知政刑，豈非至德克明哉！」

translations.literal: Where guilt is real, display clear punishment; where cases are excessive, strictly punish the prison clerks — making all under Heaven submit, and people know governance and punishment: would this not be supreme virtue and penetrating clarity!"
translations.idiomatic: Where guilt is proved, let the law be seen to strike; where charges are false, let the jailers be punished in turn. Then the empire will trust your justice, and all will understand both your mercy and your severity. Would that not be the highest expression of enlightened rule?"

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚辰朔，日南至。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengchen on the new moon, the sun reached its southern extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of the gengchen day, the winter solstice arrived.

sentences.zh: 太后享萬象神宮，赦天下。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager offered at the Palace of Myriad Forms and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sacrificed at the Palace of Myriad Forms and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 始用周正，改永昌元年十一月為載初元年正月，以十二月為臘月，夏正月為一月。

translations.literal: They began to use the Zhou calendar reckoning; changed the eleventh month of the first year of Yongchang to the first month of the first year of Zaichu; took the twelfth month as the twelfth-month month, and the summer first month as the first month.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted the Zhou calendar. The eleventh month of Yongchang 1 became the first month of Zaichu 1; the twelfth month was treated as the month of the winter sacrifice, and the old first month of the year was renumbered as the first month under the new reckoning.

sentences.zh: 以周、漢之後為二王后，舜、禹、成湯之後為三恪，周、隋之嗣同列國。

translations.literal: They made the descendants of Zhou and Han the Two Kings, the descendants of Shun, Yu, and King Cheng Tang the Three Reverent Ones, and the heirs of Zhou and Sui equal to feudal states.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the Zhou and Han houses were installed as the Two Kings; descendants of Shun, Yu, and King Tang of Shang as the Three Reverent Ones; and the surviving lines of the Zhou and Sui royal houses were ranked alongside the feudal states.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎河東宗秦客，改造「天」「地」等十二字以獻，丁亥，行之。

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Zong Qinke of Hedong reformed twelve characters including "Heaven" and "Earth" and presented them; on dinghai, they were put into use.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Qinke of Hedong, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, devised new forms for twelve characters including Heaven and Earth and presented them to the throne; on the dinghai day the new characters were adopted.

sentences.zh: 太后自名「曌」，改詔曰制。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's personal name was "Zhao"; she changed the term edict to decree.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's personal name was Zhao; she replaced the term edict with decree for imperial pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 秦客，太后從父姊之子也。

translations.literal: Qinke was the son of the Empress Dowager's father's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Qinke was the son of the Empress Dowager's aunt on her father's side.

sentences.zh: 乙未，司刑少卿周興奏除唐親屬籍。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Zhou Xing memorialized to remove the Tang imperial clan from the registry.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Zhou Xing, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, memorialized that the Tang imperial clan be struck from the official register.

sentences.zh: 臘月，辛未，以僧懷義為右衛大將軍，賜爵鄂國公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, the monk Huaiyi was made Grand General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of E.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, the monk Huaiyi was appointed Grand General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of E.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，戊子，武承嗣遷文昌左相，岑長倩遷文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品，鳳閣侍郎武攸寧為納言，邢文偉守內史，左肅政大夫、同鳳閣鸞台三品王本立罷為地官尚書。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on wuzi, Wu Chengsi was transferred to Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Palace; Cen Changqian to Right Chancellor of the Wenchang Palace and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace; Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Wu Youning became Master of Appeals; Xing Wenwei remained Interior Secretary; Left Director of the Bureau for Scrutiny Wang Benli was dismissed and made Minister of the Ministry of Territorial Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuzi, Wu Chengsi became Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Palace; Cen Changqian became Right Chancellor of the Wenchang Palace and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace; Wu Youning, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, was made Master of Appeals; Xing Wenwei remained Interior Secretary; and Wang Benli, Left Director of the Bureau for Scrutiny and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, was dismissed and made Minister of Territorial Administration.

sentences.zh: 攸寧，士擭之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Youning was the elder brother's grandson of Shi Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Youning was a grandson of Shi Kuo's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 時武承嗣、三思用事，宰相皆下之。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi held power, and all chancellors ranked below them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi held the reins of power, and every chancellor stood beneath them.

sentences.zh: 地官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台三品韋方質有疾，承嗣、三思往問之，方質據床不為禮。

translations.literal: Minister of Territorial Administration Wei Fangzhi, Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, was ill; Chengsi and Sansi went to visit him, but Fangzhi sat up in bed and did not observe ceremony toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fangzhi, Minister of Territorial Administration and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, was ill; Chengsi and Sansi came to call on him, but Fangzhi sat up in bed and refused them the usual courtesies.

sentences.zh: 或諫之，方質曰：「死生有命，大丈夫安能曲事近戚以求苟免乎！」

translations.literal: Some admonished him; Fangzhi said: "Life and death are fated — how could a true man demean himself before near kin of the throne merely to scrape by alive!"
translations.idiomatic: When others warned him, Fangzhi said, "Life and death are Heaven's decree — how could a true man grovel before the Empress Dowager's kin just to save his own skin!"

sentences.zh: 尋為周興等所構，甲午，流儋州，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed by Zhou Xing and others; on jiawu, he was exiled to Danzhou and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhou Xing and others framed him; on jiawu he was exiled to Danzhou, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，太后策貢士於洛城殿。

translations.literal: Second month, on xinyou, the Empress Dowager examined presented scholars at the Hall of Luocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou, the Empress Dowager personally examined presented scholars in the Hall of Luocheng.

sentences.zh: 貢士殿試自此始。

translations.literal: The palace examination of presented scholars began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination of degree candidates began from this occasion.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，地官尚書王本立薨。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Minister of Territorial Administration Wang Benli died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wang Benli, Minister of Territorial Administration, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁亥，特進、同鳳閣鸞台三品蘇良嗣薨。

translations.literal: Third month, on dinghai, Special Advanced Su Liangsi, Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dinghai, Su Liangsi, Special Advanced and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，春官尚書、同平章事范履冰坐嘗舉犯逆者，下獄死。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on dingsi, Minister of the Ministry of Rites Fan Lübing, Co-equal Chancellor, was charged with having once recommended a rebel; he was thrown into prison and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi, Fan Lübing, Minister of Rites and Co-equal Chancellor, was accused of having once recommended a man later convicted of treason; he was imprisoned and died in custody.

sentences.zh: 醴泉人侯思止，始以賣餅為業，後事游擊將軍高元禮為僕，素詭譎無賴。

translations.literal: Hou Sizhi of Liquan first made his living selling cakes; later he served the mobile corps general Gao Yuanli as a servant. By nature he was crafty and an unscrupulous scoundrel.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sizhi of Liquan had first earned his bread selling cakes; later he entered the household of the mobile corps general Gao Yuanli as a servant. He was by nature cunning and utterly without scruple.

sentences.zh: 恆州刺史裴貞杖一判司，判司使思止告貞與舒王元名謀反，秋，七月，辛巳，元名坐廢，徙和州，壬午，殺其子豫章王但；

translations.literal: The prefect of Heng Prefecture Pei Zhen beat a judicial aide; the aide had Sizhi report that Zhen was plotting rebellion with Prince Shu Yuanming. Autumn, seventh month, on xinsi, Yuanming was stripped of rank and moved to Hezhou; on renwu his son the Prince of Yuzhang Dan was killed;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhen, prefect of Heng Prefecture, beat a judicial aide; the aide had Sizhi accuse Zhen of plotting rebellion with Prince Shu Yuanming. In autumn, the seventh month, on xinsi Yuanming was deposed and exiled to Hezhou; on renwu his son Dan, Prince of Yuzhang, was executed;

sentences.zh: 貞亦族滅。

translations.literal: Zhen's entire clan was also exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhen's entire clan was exterminated as well.

sentences.zh: 擢思止為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: Sizhi was promoted to mobile corps general.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi was promoted to mobile corps general.

sentences.zh: 時告密者往往得五品，思止求為御史，太后曰：「卿不識字，豈堪御史！」

translations.literal: At the time informers often received fifth rank; Sizhi asked to be made censor. The Empress Dowager said: "You cannot read — how could you serve as censor!"
translations.idiomatic: Informers at the time often received fifth rank; Sizhi asked to be made a censor. The Empress Dowager said, "You cannot read — how could you serve as censor!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獬豸何嘗識字？

translations.literal: He replied: "Did the xiezhi ever know how to read?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Did the xiezhi ever know how to read?

sentences.zh: 但能觸邪耳。」

translations.literal: It only had to touch the wicked."
translations.idiomatic: It only had to touch the wicked."

sentences.zh: 太后悅，即以為朝散大夫、侍御史。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased and made him Gentlemen for Court Discussion and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was delighted and appointed him Gentlemen for Court Discussion and Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 他日，太后以先所籍沒宅賜之，思止不受，曰：「臣惡反逆之人，不願居其宅。」

translations.literal: Another day the Empress Dowager bestowed on him a house previously confiscated; Sizhi refused, saying: "Your subject hates rebels and will not live in their house."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the Empress Dowager gave him a house that had earlier been confiscated; Sizhi refused it, saying, "I loathe traitors and will not live in their dwelling."

sentences.zh: 太后益賞之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 衡水人王弘義，素無行，嘗從鄰舍乞瓜，不與，乃告縣官瓜田中有白兔。

translations.literal: Wang Hongyi of Hengshui was by nature without integrity. Once he begged melons from a neighbor, who refused; he then reported to the county magistrate that there was a white rabbit in the melon field.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongyi of Hengshui was a man of bad character. Once he begged melons from a neighbor; when the neighbor refused, he reported to the county magistrate that a white rabbit had appeared in the melon patch.

sentences.zh: 縣官使人搜捕，蹂踐瓜田立盡。

translations.literal: The county magistrate sent men to search and capture it; they trampled the melon field until it was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate sent men to hunt for it, and they trampled the melon field until not a plant was left standing.

sentences.zh: 又游趙、貝，見閭裡耆老作邑齋，遂告以謀反，殺二百餘人，擢授游擊將軍，俄遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He also traveled through Zhao and Bei; seeing village elders holding a communal feast, he reported them for plotting rebellion; more than two hundred were killed. He was promoted to mobile corps general and soon transferred to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through Zhao and Bei, he saw village elders holding a communal feast and reported them for plotting rebellion; more than two hundred people were killed. He was promoted to mobile corps general and soon made a palace censor.

sentences.zh: 或告勝州都督王安仁謀反，敕弘義按之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Sheng Prefecture Commandant Wang Anren was plotting rebellion; Hongyi was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Wang Anren, Commandant of Sheng Prefecture, was plotting rebellion, Hongyi was ordered to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 安仁不服，弘義即於枷上刎其首；

translations.literal: Anren denied guilt; Hongyi immediately cut his throat on the cangue;
translations.idiomatic: Anren denied the charge; Hongyi immediately cut his throat while he stood in the cangue;

sentences.zh: 又捕其子，適至，亦刎其首，函之以歸。

translations.literal: He also seized his son, who had just arrived; he cut his head off too, boxed them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized Anren's son, who had just arrived; he cut off his head as well, boxed both heads, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 道過汾州，司馬毛公與之對食，須臾，叱毛公下階，斬之，槍揭其首入洛，見者無不震慄。

translations.literal: Passing through Fenzhou, he was dining opposite Assistant Commander Mao; in a moment he shouted Mao down the steps and beheaded him, speared the head and carried it into Luoyang — all who saw it trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he passed through Fenzhou and was sharing a meal with Assistant Commander Mao; in a moment he shouted Mao down the steps and beheaded him, then speared the head and carried it into Luoyang. All who saw it were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 時置制獄於麗景門內，入是獄者，非死不出，弘義戲呼為「例竟門」。

translations.literal: Special prisons were set up inside Lizijing Gate; whoever entered those prisons did not leave except dead. Hongyi jokingly called it the "Gate of Cases Closed."
translations.idiomatic: Special prisons had been set up inside Lizijing Gate; whoever entered them left only in death. Hongyi mockingly called it the "Gate Where Cases Are Closed."

sentences.zh: 朝士人人自危，相見莫敢交言，道路以目。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen all lived in dread; when they met one another none dared speak; they communicated only with their eyes in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Every court gentleman lived in dread; when they met one another none dared speak aloud, and in the streets they communicated only with their eyes.

sentences.zh: 或因入朝密遭掩捕，每朝，輒與家人訣曰：「未知復相見否？」

translations.literal: Some were secretly seized on their way to court; before every court session they would take leave of their families saying: "Who knows whether we shall meet again?"
translations.idiomatic: Some were secretly seized on their way to court; before each session they would take leave of their families, saying, "Who knows whether we shall ever meet again?"

sentences.zh: 時法官競為深酷，唯司刑丞徐有功、杜景儉獨存平恕，被告者皆曰：「遇來、侯必死，遇徐、杜必生。」

translations.literal: At the time judges competed in severity; only Vice Directors of the Ministry of Punishments Xu Yougong and Du Jingjian alone maintained fairness and clemency. The accused all said: "If we meet Lai or Hou we must die; if we meet Xu or Du we shall live."
translations.idiomatic: Judges at the time vied in cruelty; only Vice Directors of the Ministry of Punishments Xu Yougong and Du Jingjian held to fairness and mercy. The accused all said, "Meet Lai or Hou and you die; meet Xu or Du and you live."

sentences.zh: 有功，文遠之孫也，名弘敏，以字行。

translations.literal: Yougong was the grandson of Wen Yuan; his name was Hongmin, but he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong was a grandson of Wen Yuan; his given name was Hongmin, but he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 初為蒲州司法，以寬為治，不施敲樸，吏相約有犯徐司法杖者，眾共斥之。

translations.literal: At first he was judicial officer of Pu Prefecture; he governed with leniency and never applied the beating staff. The clerks agreed among themselves that whoever would cause Judicial Officer Xu to use the staff would be jointly rebuked by all.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as judicial officer of Pu Prefecture, governing with leniency and never applying the beating staff. The clerks agreed among themselves that whoever forced Judicial Officer Xu to raise the staff would be rebuked by the whole office.

sentences.zh: 迨官滿，不杖一人，職事亦修。

translations.literal: When his term ended he had beaten not a single person, yet his official duties were also well performed.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he had beaten not a single person, yet his official duties were fully discharged.

sentences.zh: 累遷司刑丞，酷吏所誣構者，有功皆為直之，前後所活數十百家。

translations.literal: Promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, all whom the harsh officials falsely implicated, Yougong straightened out their cases; in all he saved several tens of families.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, he overturned every case the harsh officials had fabricated, saving several tens of families in all.

sentences.zh: 嘗廷爭獄事，太后厲色詰之，左右為戰慄，有功神色不撓，爭之彌切。

translations.literal: Once he disputed a prison case in open court; the Empress Dowager sternly questioned him; those beside her trembled with fear, yet Yougong's expression did not waver and he argued all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Once he disputed a prison case in open court; the Empress Dowager questioned him with a fierce countenance, and those beside her trembled, yet Yougong's expression never changed and he argued all the more urgently.

sentences.zh: 太后雖好殺，知有功正直，甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: Though the Empress Dowager loved killing, knowing Yougong was upright she greatly respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Empress Dowager loved bloodshed, knowing Yougong's integrity she deeply respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 景儉，武邑人也。

translations.literal: Jingjian was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian was a native of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 司刑丞滎陽李日知亦尚平恕。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Li Rizhi of Xingyang also valued fairness and clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi of Xingyang, also a Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, likewise prized fairness and clemency.

sentences.zh: 少卿胡元禮欲殺一囚，日知以為不可，往複數日，元禮怒曰：「元禮不離刑曹，此囚終無生理！」

translations.literal: Assistant Director Hu Yuanli wished to kill a prisoner; Rizhi thought it impossible. They exchanged arguments for several days; Yuanli angrily said: "So long as Yuanli does not leave the punishment office, this prisoner will ultimately have no way to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Hu Yuanli wanted to execute a prisoner; Rizhi held that it could not be done. They argued back and forth for days until Yuanli burst out, "So long as Yuanli remains in the punishment office, this man will never leave it alive!"

sentences.zh: 日知曰：「日知不離刑曹，此囚終無死法！」

translations.literal: Rizhi said: "So long as Rizhi does not leave the punishment office, this prisoner will ultimately have no way to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi replied, "So long as Rizhi remains in the punishment office, this man will never be put to death!"

sentences.zh: 竟以兩狀列上，日知果直。

translations.literal: In the end they submitted two separate memorials; Rizhi was indeed vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they submitted two separate memorials to the throne; Rizhi was vindicated.

sentences.zh: 東魏國寺僧法明等撰《大雲經》四卷，表上之，言太后乃彌勒佛下生，當代唐為閻浮提主；

translations.literal: Monks Faming and others of the Eastern Wei Kingdom Temple compiled four scrolls of the Dayun Sutra and memorialized it upward, saying the Empress Dowager was Maitreya Buddha incarnated, to replace Tang as lord of Jambudvipa;
translations.idiomatic: The monks Faming and others of the Eastern Wei Kingdom Temple compiled four scrolls of the Dayun Sutra and presented them to the throne, declaring that the Empress Dowager was Maitreya Buddha incarnate, destined to replace the Tang and rule Jambudvipa;

sentences.zh: 制頒於天下。

translations.literal: The decree was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣使周興羅告隋州刺史澤王上金、舒州刺史許王素節謀反，征詣行在。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi had Zhou Xing weave accusations that Ze Wang Shangjin, prefect of Sui Prefecture, and Xu Wang Sujie, prefect of Shu Prefecture, were plotting rebellion; they were summoned to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi had Zhou Xing fabricate charges that Ze Wang Shangjin, prefect of Sui Prefecture, and Xu Wang Sujie, prefect of Shu Prefecture, were plotting rebellion; both were summoned to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 素節發舒州，聞遭喪哭者，歎曰：「病死何可得，乃更哭邪！」

translations.literal: Sujie set out from Shu Prefecture; hearing people wailing for the bereaved he sighed: "Death by illness — who could hope for that — and you still weep!"
translations.idiomatic: Sujie set out from Shu Prefecture; hearing mourners wailing along the road, he sighed, "Who can hope to die of illness these days — and yet you still weep!"

sentences.zh: 丁亥，至龍門，縊殺之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, when he reached Longmen, he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, when he reached Longmen, he was strangled to death.

sentences.zh: 上金自殺。

translations.literal: Shangjin killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjin took his own life.

sentences.zh: 悉誅其諸子及支黨。

translations.literal: All their sons and followers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: All their sons and followers were executed.

sentences.zh: 太后欲以太平公主妻其伯父士讓之孫攸暨，攸暨時為右衛中郎將，太后潛使人殺其妻而妻之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to marry Princess Taiping to Wu Youji, grandson of her uncle Shi Rang; Youji was then a middle commander of the Right Guard; the Empress Dowager secretly had his wife killed and gave him the princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to marry Princess Taiping to Wu Youji, grandson of her uncle Shi Rang. Youji was then a middle commander of the Right Guard; the Empress Dowager secretly had his wife killed and gave him the princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 公主方額廣頤，多權略，太后以為類己，寵愛特厚，常與密議天下事。

translations.literal: The princess had a broad forehead and full jowls, and much shrewdness in power; the Empress Dowager thought her like herself, favored her with special warmth, and often secretly deliberated on affairs of the realm with her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had a broad forehead and full cheeks and was skilled in intrigue; the Empress Dowager saw her own likeness in her, favored her above all others, and often consulted with her in secret on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 舊制，食邑，諸王不過千戶，公主不過三百五十戶；

translations.literal: Under the old system for fief households, princes received no more than a thousand households, princesses no more than three hundred fifty;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system of fief households, princes received no more than a thousand households and princesses no more than three hundred and fifty;

sentences.zh: 太平食邑獨累加至三千戶。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping's fief alone was repeatedly increased until it reached three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping's fief alone was repeatedly increased until it reached three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲寅，殺太子少保、納言裴居道；

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiayin, they killed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and Master of Appeals Pei Judao;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiayin, Pei Judao, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and Master of Appeals, was executed;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，殺尚書左丞張行廉。

translations.literal: On guihai, they killed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Zhang Xinglian.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Zhang Xinglian, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, was executed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，殺南安王穎等宗室十二人，又鞭殺故太子賢二子，唐之宗室於是殆盡矣，其幼弱存者亦流嶺南，又誅其親黨數百家。

translations.literal: On xinwei, they killed twelve members of the imperial clan including Prince Nan'an Ying, and also flogged to death the two sons of the former Crown Prince Xian; the Tang imperial clan was thus nearly exterminated, and those young and weak who survived were also exiled to Lingnan; several hundred of their kin and partisans were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, twelve members of the imperial clan including Prince Nan'an Ying were killed, and the two sons of the former Crown Prince Xian were flogged to death. The Tang imperial house was now all but wiped out; those young and weak who survived were exiled to Lingnan, and several hundred of their kin and partisans were put to death.

sentences.zh: 惟千金長公主以巧媚得全，自請為太后女，仍改姓武氏；

translations.literal: Only Princess Qianjin survived through artful flattery; she asked to become the Empress Dowager's daughter and also changed her surname to Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Only Princess Qianjin survived, saved by artful flattery; she asked to be adopted as the Empress Dowager's daughter and took the surname Wu;

sentences.zh: 太后愛之，更號延安大長公主。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager loved her and gave her the new title Grand Princess of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager doted on her and gave her the new title Grand Princess of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙子，侍御史汲人傅遊藝帥關中百姓九百餘人詣闕上表，請改國號曰周，賜皇帝姓武氏，太后不許；

translations.literal: Ninth month, on bingzi, Attending Censor Fu Youyi of Ji led more than nine hundred commoners of Guanzhong to the palace gate with a memorial asking to change the dynastic name to Zhou and give the emperor the surname Wu; the Empress Dowager did not consent;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Fu Youyi of Ji, an Attending Censor, led more than nine hundred commoners from Guanzhong to the palace gate with a memorial asking that the dynastic name be changed to Zhou and the emperor be given the surname Wu; the Empress Dowager refused;

sentences.zh: 擢遊藝為給事中。

translations.literal: Youyi was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 於是百官及帝室宗戚、遠近百姓、四夷酋長、沙門、道士合六萬餘人，俱上表如遊藝所請，皇帝亦上表自請賜姓武氏。

translations.literal: Then officials, imperial clansmen, distant commoners, barbarian chieftains, monks and Taoists totaling more than sixty thousand all submitted memorials as Youyi had requested; the emperor also submitted a memorial asking to be given the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials, imperial clansmen, commoners from near and far, barbarian chieftains, monks, and Taoists — more than sixty thousand in all — submitted memorials making the same request; the emperor too memorialized, asking to be given the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，群臣上言：「有鳳皇自明堂飛入上陽宮，還集左台梧桐之上，久之，飛東南去；

translations.literal: On wuyin, the assembled ministers reported: "A phoenix flew from the Bright Hall into Shangyang Palace, then gathered on the phoenix tree of the Left Terrace; after a long while it flew away to the southeast;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the assembled ministers reported, "A phoenix flew from the Bright Hall into Shangyang Palace, then alighted on the phoenix tree of the Left Terrace; after a long while it flew away toward the southeast;

sentences.zh: 及赤雀數萬集朝堂。

translations.literal: and tens of thousands of red sparrows gathered at the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: and tens of thousands of red sparrows gathered in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，太后可皇帝及群臣之請。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Empress Dowager approved the emperor's and the ministers' request.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Empress Dowager accepted the petition of the emperor and the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 壬午，御則天數，赦天下，以唐為周，改元。

translations.literal: On renwu, she assumed the imperial seat under the Zetian numeral system, amnestied all under Heaven, replaced Tang with Zhou, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu she took the throne under the Zetian numeral system, proclaimed a general amnesty, replaced Tang with Zhou, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上尊號曰聖神皇帝，以皇帝為皇嗣，賜姓武氏；

translations.literal: On yiyou, they honored her as Holy Divine Emperor, made the emperor imperial heir, and gave him the surname Wu;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou she was honored as Holy Divine Emperor; the emperor was made imperial heir and given the surname Wu;

sentences.zh: 以皇太子為皇孫。

translations.literal: The crown prince was made imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was demoted to imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，立武氏七廟於神都，追尊周文王曰始祖文皇帝，妣姒氏曰文定皇后，平王少子武曰睿祖康皇帝，妣姜氏曰康惠皇后；

translations.literal: On bingxu, they established the seven temples of the Wu clan in the Divine Capital; posthumously honored King Wen of Zhou as Founding Ancestor Literary Emperor, his consort the Si clan as Literary Fixed Empress, the youngest son Wu of King Ping as Sagacious Ancestor Kang Emperor, his consort the Jiang clan as Kang Kind Empress;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the seven temples of the Wu clan were established in the Divine Capital; King Wen of Zhou was posthumously honored as Founding Ancestor Literary Emperor and his consort of the Si clan as Literary Fixed Empress; Wu, youngest son of King Ping, as Sagacious Ancestor Kang Emperor and his consort of the Jiang clan as Kang Kind Empress;

sentences.zh: 太原靖王曰嚴祖成皇帝，妣曰成莊皇后；

translations.literal: the Prince of Taiyuan Jing was called Stern Ancestor Cheng Emperor, his consort called Cheng Solemn Empress;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Taiyuan Jing was posthumously titled Stern Ancestor Cheng Emperor and his consort Cheng Solemn Empress;

sentences.zh: 趙肅恭王曰肅祖章敬皇帝，魏義康王曰烈祖昭安皇帝，周安成王曰顯祖文穆皇帝，忠孝太皇曰太祖孝明高皇帝，妣皆如考謚，稱皇后。

translations.literal: the Prince of Zhao Su Gong was called Reverent Ancestor Zhangjing Emperor, the Prince of Wei Yi Kang was called Fierce Ancestor Zhao'an Emperor, the Prince of Zhou An Cheng was called Illustrious Ancestor Wenmu Emperor, the Filial and Loyal Grand Emperor was called Great Ancestor Xiaoming Gao Emperor; the consorts all received posthumous titles matching their husbands and were called empresses.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Zhao Su Gong was titled Reverent Ancestor Zhangjing Emperor; the Prince of Wei Yi Kang, Fierce Ancestor Zhao'an Emperor; the Prince of Zhou An Cheng, Illustrious Ancestor Wenmu Emperor; and the Filial and Loyal Grand Emperor, Great Ancestor Xiaoming Gao Emperor — each consort receiving a posthumous title to match her husband and being styled empress.

sentences.zh: 立武承嗣為魏王，三思為梁王，攸寧為建昌王，士擭兄孫攸歸、重規、載德、攸暨、懿宗、嗣宗、攸宜、攸望、攸緒、攸止皆為郡王，諸姑姊皆為長公主。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi was established as Prince of Wei, Sansi as Prince of Liang, Youning as Prince of Jianchang; Yougui, Chonggui, Zaide, Youji, Yizong, Sizong, Youyi, Youwang, Youxu, and Youzhi — grandsons of Shi Kuo's elder brother — were all made princes of commanderies; all paternal aunts and elder sisters were made grand princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, Wu Sansi as Prince of Liang, and Wu Youning as Prince of Jianchang; Yougui, Chonggui, Zaide, Youji, Yizong, Sizong, Youyi, Youwang, Youxu, and Youzhi — grandsons of Shi Kuo's elder brother — were all made commandery princes; and every paternal aunt and elder sister of the Wu clan was made a grand princess.

sentences.zh: 又以司賓卿溧陽史務滋為納言，鳳閣侍郎宗秦客檢校內史，給事中傅遊藝為鸞台侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Shi Wuzi of Liyang, Director of the Ministry of Guests, was also made Master of Appeals; Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Zong Qinke was made Acting Interior Secretary; Attendant Gentleman Fu Youyi was made Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuzi of Liyang, Director of the Ministry of Guests, was made Master of Appeals; Zong Qinke, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, was made Acting Interior Secretary; and Fu Youyi, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, was made Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 遊藝與岑長倩、右玉鈐衛大將軍張虔勖、左金吾大將軍丘神勣、侍御史來子珣等並賜姓武。

translations.literal: Youyi, together with Cen Changqian, Right Jade Talisman Guard Grand General Zhang Qianxu, Left Golden Crow Guard Grand General Qiu Shenji, Attending Censor Lai Zixun, and others, were all granted the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi, together with Cen Changqian, Zhang Qianxu, Grand General of the Right Jade Talisman Guard, Qiu Shenji, Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, Lai Zixun, Attending Censor, and others, were all granted the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 秦客潛勸太后革命，故首為內史。

translations.literal: Qinke had secretly urged the Empress Dowager to change the dynasty, and therefore was first made Interior Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Qinke had secretly urged the Empress Dowager to seize the throne, and for that reason was the first appointed Interior Secretary.

sentences.zh: 遊藝期年之中歷衣青、綠、朱、紫，時人謂之四時仕宦。

translations.literal: Within a single year Youyi passed through green, green-red, red, and purple robes; people of the time called it the four-season official career.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year Youyi passed through every rank of official robe — green, green-red, red, and purple — and people called it a career in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 敕改州為郡；

translations.literal: An edict ordered prefectures changed to commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that prefectures be renamed commanderies;

sentences.zh: 或謂太后曰：「陛下始革命而廢州，不祥。」

translations.literal: Someone told the Empress Dowager: "Your Majesty has just changed the dynasty and abolishes prefectures — ill omen."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the Empress Dowager, "Your Majesty has just changed the dynasty, yet now abolishes prefectures — this is an ill omen."

sentences.zh: 太后遽追止之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager immediately revoked the order.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager immediately revoked the order.

sentences.zh: 命史務滋等十人存撫諸道。

translations.literal: She ordered Shi Wuzi and ten others to tour and reassure the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: She dispatched Shi Wuzi and nine others to tour the circuits and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太后立兄孫延基等六人為郡王。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Empress Dowager established six grandsons including Yanji as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Empress Dowager enfeoffed six of her brother's grandsons, including Yanji, as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，檢校內史宗秦客坐贓貶遵化尉，弟楚客、晉卿亦以奸贓流嶺外。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jiazi, Acting Interior Secretary Zong Qinke was demoted to Commandant of Dunhua for corruption; his younger brothers Chu Ke and Jin Qing were also exiled beyond the mountains for graft and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, Zong Qinke, Acting Interior Secretary, was demoted to Commandant of Dunhua on charges of corruption; his younger brothers Chu Ke and Jin Qing were also exiled beyond the mountains for graft.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，殺流人韋方質。

translations.literal: On dingmao, they killed the exiled Wei Fangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the exiled Wei Fangzhi was executed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，內史邢文偉坐附會宗秦客貶珍州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Interior Secretary Xing Wenwei was demoted to prefect of Zhen Prefecture for associating himself with Zong Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Xing Wenwei, Interior Secretary, was demoted to prefect of Zhen Prefecture for having sided with Zong Qinke.

sentences.zh: 頃之，有制使至州，文偉以為誅己，遽自縊死。

translations.literal: Before long an imperial commissioner arrived at the prefecture; Wenwei thought he had come to execute him and immediately hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial commissioner arrived at the prefecture; Wenwei took it as a death warrant and immediately hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 壬申，敕兩京諸州各置大雲寺一區，藏《大雲經》，使僧升高座講解，其撰疏僧雲宣等九人皆賜爵縣公，仍賜紫袈裟、銀龜袋。

translations.literal: On renshen, an edict ordered that in each prefecture of the two capitals one Dayun Temple be established, storing the Dayun Sutra, with monks raised to the high seat to expound it; the nine monks who wrote commentaries including Yun Xuan were all enfeoffed as county dukes and also given purple kasayas and silver tortoise pouches.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict ordered that every prefecture in the two capitals establish a Dayun Temple housing the Dayun Sutra, with monks appointed to the high seat to expound it; the nine monks who had written commentaries, including Yun Xuan, were all enfeoffed as county dukes and given purple kasayas and silver tortoise pouches.

sentences.zh: 制天下武氏鹹蠲課役。

translations.literal: A decree wholly exempted all under Heaven of the Wu surname from taxes and corvee.
translations.idiomatic: A decree wholly exempted everyone bearing the surname Wu from taxes and corvee labor.

sentences.zh: 西突厥十姓，自垂拱以來，為東突厥所侵掠，散亡略盡。

translations.literal: The ten tribes of the Western Turks, since the Chuigong era, had been raided by the Eastern Turks, scattered and lost almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The ten tribes of the Western Turks, since the Chuigong era, had been raided by the Eastern Turks until they were scattered and all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 濛池都護繼往絕可汗斛瑟羅收其餘眾六七萬人入居內地，拜左衛大將軍，改號竭忠事主可汗。

translations.literal: Mengchi Protector Qibi Heluo, Khan Jiwangjue, gathered the remaining followers of sixty or seventy thousand and settled them within the interior; he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard and his title was changed to Khan Who Exhausts Loyalty in Serving the Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heluo, Khan Jiwangjue and Protector of Mengchi, gathered the sixty or seventy thousand survivors and settled them within the empire; he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard and given the new title Khan Who Exhausts Loyalty in Serving the Lord.

sentences.zh: 道州刺史李行褒兄弟為酷吏所陷，當族，秋官郎中徐有功固爭不能得。

translations.literal: Li Xing'ao and his brothers of Daozhou were framed by harsh officials and were due for clan extermination; Autumn Office Bureau Director Xu Yougong firmly argued but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing'ao and his brothers of Daozhou were framed by harsh officials and sentenced to clan extermination; Xu Yougong, Bureau Director of the Autumn Office, argued fiercely on their behalf but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 秋官侍郎周興奏有功故出反囚，當斬，太后雖不許，亦免有功官；

translations.literal: Autumn Office Vice Director Zhou Xing memorialized that Yougong had deliberately released rebel prisoners and deserved decapitation; though the Empress Dowager did not consent, she still dismissed Yougong from office;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing, Vice Director of the Autumn Office, memorialized that Yougong had deliberately released rebel prisoners and deserved execution; though the Empress Dowager did not consent to his death, she still stripped Yougong of office;

sentences.zh: 然太后雅重有功，久之，復起為侍御史。

translations.literal: Yet the Empress Dowager greatly esteemed Yougong; after a long while she restored him as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager nevertheless held Yougong in high regard, and after some time restored him to office as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 有功伏地流涕固辭曰：「臣聞鹿走山林而命懸包廚，勢使之然也。

translations.literal: Yougong prostrated himself, weeping, and firmly declined, saying: "Your subject has heard that when a deer runs in the mountains and forests its life hangs over the kitchen — the situation makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong prostrated himself in tears and firmly declined, saying, "I have heard that when a deer runs free in the hills and forests, its life still hangs over the butcher's block — that is what circumstance does.

sentences.zh: 陛下以臣為法官，臣不敢枉陛下法，必死是官矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty appoints your subject as a judge; your subject dares not bend Your Majesty's law — he must die in this office."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has made me a judge; I dare not bend your law, and I am sure to die in this office."

sentences.zh: 太后固授之，遠近聞者相賀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager still invested him with the office; those near and far who heard of it congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager insisted on appointing him anyway, and all who heard the news, near and far, rejoiced for him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以右衛大將軍泉獻誠為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: That year, Right Guard Grand General Quan Xiancheng was made Left Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: That year Quan Xiancheng, Grand General of the Right Guard, was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 太后出金寶，命選南北牙善射者五人賭之，獻誠第一，以讓右玉鈐衛大將軍薛咄摩，咄摩復讓獻誠。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager brought out gold and jewels and ordered that five skilled archers from the northern and southern guards be chosen to compete; Xiancheng came first and yielded the prize to Right Jade Talisman Guard Grand General Xue Duomo, and Duomo in turn yielded it back to Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager brought out gold and jewels and ordered a contest among five skilled archers chosen from the northern and southern guards. Xiancheng took first place and yielded the prize to Xue Duomo, Grand General of the Right Jade Talisman Guard, who in turn yielded it back to Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 獻誠乃奏言：「陛下令選善射者，今多非漢官，竊恐四夷輕漢，請停此射。」

translations.literal: Xiancheng then memorialized: "Your Majesty ordered skilled archers to be chosen, but many of those selected now are not Han officials; your subject fears the four barbarians will look down on Han, and asks that this archery contest be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng then memorialized, "Your Majesty ordered skilled archers to be chosen, but many of those selected are not Han officials. I fear the four barbarians will look down on the Han — I beg that this contest be stopped."

sentences.zh: 太后善而從之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager approved and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager approved and followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 正月，癸酉朔，太后始受尊號於萬象神宮，旗幟尚赤。

translations.literal: First month, on the new moon of guiyou, the Empress Dowager first received her honorific title at the Palace of Myriad Forms; banners and flags favored red.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on the new moon of the guiyou day, the Empress Dowager first received her honorific title at the Palace of Myriad Forms, with banners and flags in red.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，改置社稷於神都。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the altars of soil and grain were moved and established in the Divine Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the altars of soil and grain were reestablished in the Divine Capital.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，納武氏神主於太廟；

translations.literal: On xinsi, the spirit tablets of the Wu clan were installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the spirit tablets of the Wu clan were installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 唐太廟之在長安者，更命曰享德廟。

translations.literal: the Tang Imperial Ancestral Temple that remained in Chang'an was renamed the Temple of Honored Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the Tang ancestral temple in Chang'an was renamed the Temple of Honored Virtue.

sentences.zh: 四時唯享高祖已下三廟，餘四室皆閉不享。

translations.literal: In the four seasons only the three temples from the High Ancestor downward were offered to; the remaining four chambers were all closed and not offered to.
translations.idiomatic: Through the four seasons only the three temples from the High Ancestor downward received offerings; the remaining four chambers were closed and left unhonored.

sentences.zh: 又改長安崇先廟為崇尊廟。

translations.literal: The Chongxian Temple in Chang'an was also renamed the Chongzun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongxian Temple in Chang'an was likewise renamed the Chongzun Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，日南至，大享明堂，祀昊天上帝，百神從祀，武氏祖宗配享，唐三帝亦同配。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the sun reached its southern extreme; a great offering was made in the Bright Hall, sacrificing to the August Heaven God, with the hundred spirits following in sacrifice; the Wu clan ancestors were paired in the offering, and the three Tang emperors were paired likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the winter solstice, a great sacrifice was held in the Bright Hall to the August Heaven God, with the hundred spirits in attendance. The Wu clan ancestors were paired in the rite, and the three Tang emperors were paired as well.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞知大夫事李嗣真以酷吏縱橫，上疏，以為：「今告事紛紜，虛多實少，恐有凶慝陰謀離間陛下君臣。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief acting as Grand Censor Li Sizhen, because harsh officials ran rampant, submitted a memorial saying: "Reports of offenses now come in profusion; false ones outnumber true ones. Your subject fears there are wicked men plotting in secret to drive a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhen, Censor-in-Chief acting as Grand Censor, submitted a memorial against the rampant harsh officials, saying, "Reports of offenses now flood in — false ones far outnumber true ones. I fear wicked men are plotting in secret to drive a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers.

sentences.zh: 古者獄成，公卿參聽，王必三宥，然後行刑。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when a case was complete, the high ministers jointly heard it; the king had to pardon three times before carrying out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a case was complete the high ministers jointly heard it, and the king had to pardon three times before punishment could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 比日獄官單車奉使，推鞫既定，法家依斷，不令重推；

translations.literal: In recent days prison officials go out alone on commission; once interrogation is settled the legalists decide according to the law and do not allow re-examination;
translations.idiomatic: Nowadays prison officials go out alone on commission; once interrogation is finished the legalists decide the case and allow no re-examination;

sentences.zh: 或臨時專決，不復聞奏。

translations.literal: sometimes they decide on the spot by special authority and no longer report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes they decide on the spot by special authority without reporting to the throne.

sentences.zh: 如此，則權由臣下，非審慎之法，倘有冤濫，何由可知！

translations.literal: If it is like this, then power lies with subordinates — this is not a method of careful deliberation. If there are wrongful condemnations, how could one know!
translations.idiomatic: If this is allowed, power rests with subordinates — this is no method of careful justice. If innocents are condemned, how will anyone know!

sentences.zh: 況以九品之官專命推覆，操殺生之柄，竊人主之威，按覆既不在秋官，省審復不由門下，國之利器，輕以假人，恐為社稷之禍。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to let officials of the ninth rank have sole commission to investigate and overturn cases, wielding the power of life and death and usurping the sovereign's authority — investigation is no longer in the Autumn Office, and review is no longer through the Gate Department. The state's sharp instruments are lightly lent to others; your subject fears this will be a calamity for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to let officials of the ninth rank have sole commission to investigate cases, wielding the power of life and death and usurping the sovereign's authority — with investigation no longer in the Autumn Office and review no longer through the Gate Department — is to lend the state's sharp instruments lightly to others. I fear this will bring calamity upon the realm."

sentences.zh: 太后不聽。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 饒阻尉姚貞亮等數百人表請上尊號曰上聖大神皇帝，不許。

translations.literal: Commandant of Raozu Yao Zhenliang and several hundred others submitted a memorial asking that the honorific title Supreme Sage Great Spirit Emperor be granted; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zhenliang, Commandant of Raozu, and several hundred others submitted a memorial asking that the honorific title Supreme Sage Great Spirit Emperor be granted; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 侍御史來子珣誣尚衣奉御劉行感兄弟謀反，皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Lai Zixun falsely accused Palace Wardrobe Attendant Liu Xinggan and his brothers of plotting rebellion; all were executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zixun, Attending Censor, falsely accused Liu Xinggan, Palace Wardrobe Attendant, and his brothers of plotting rebellion; all were executed.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，地官尚書武思文及朝集使二千八百人表請封中岳。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Minister of Territorial Administration Wu Siwen and twenty-eight hundred court assembly envoys submitted a memorial asking to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wu Siwen, Minister of Territorial Administration, and twenty-eight hundred court assembly envoys submitted a memorial asking to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 己亥，廢唐興寧、永康、隱陵署官，唯量置守戶。

translations.literal: On jihai, the offices of Tang's Xingning, Yongkang, and Yinling tombs were abolished; only tomb-keeper households were allotted as needed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the offices of the Tang tombs Xingning, Yongkang, and Yinling were abolished, and only tomb-keeper households were allotted as needed.

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍丘神勣以罪誅。

translations.literal: Left Golden Crow Guard Grand General Qiu Shenji was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shenji, Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 納言史務滋與來俊臣同鞫劉行感獄，俊臣奏務滋與行感親密，意欲寢其反狀。

translations.literal: Master of Appeals Shi Wuzi jointly interrogated the Liu Xinggan case with Lai Jun Chen; Jun Chen memorialized that Wuzi was intimate with Xinggan and intended to suppress evidence of his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuzi, Master of Appeals, jointly interrogated the Liu Xinggan case with Lai Jun Chen. Jun Chen memorialized that Wuzi was intimate with Xinggan and intended to suppress evidence of treason.

sentences.zh: 太后命俊臣並推之，庚子，務滋恐懼自殺。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Jun Chen to investigate Wuzi as well; on gengzi, Wuzi, in fear, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered Jun Chen to investigate Wuzi as well. On gengzi Wuzi, in terror, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 或告文昌右丞周興與丘神勣通謀，太后命來俊臣鞫之，俊臣與興方推事對食，謂興曰：「囚多不承，當為何法？」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Wenchang Palace Right Assistant Director Zhou Xing was in conspiracy with Qiu Shenji; the Empress Dowager ordered Lai Jun Chen to interrogate him. Jun Chen and Xing were just then investigating cases over a shared meal, and Jun Chen said to Xing: "Prisoners often do not confess — what method should be used?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Zhou Xing, Right Assistant Director of the Wenchang Palace, was in conspiracy with Qiu Shenji. The Empress Dowager ordered Lai Jun Chen to interrogate him. Jun Chen and Xing were investigating cases over a shared meal when Jun Chen asked Xing, "Prisoners often refuse to confess — what method should be used?"

sentences.zh: 興曰：「此甚易取。

translations.literal: Xing said: "This is very easy to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "That is very easily done.

sentences.zh: 取大甕，以炭四周炙之，令囚入中，何事不承！」

translations.literal: Take a large jar, heat it all around with charcoal, and make the prisoner enter it — what matter would he not confess!"
translations.idiomatic: Take a large jar, heat it all around with charcoal, and put the prisoner inside — what would he not confess!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃索大甕，火圍如興法，因起謂興曰：「有內狀推史，請兄入此甕。」

translations.literal: Jun Chen then sent for a large jar and surrounded it with fire as Xing's method prescribed; then he rose and said to Xing: "There is an imperial order to investigate the censor — please, elder brother, enter this jar."
translations.idiomatic: Jun Chen then sent for a large jar and surrounded it with fire exactly as Xing had described; then he rose and said to Xing, "There is an imperial order to investigate the censor — please, elder brother, enter this jar."

sentences.zh: 興惶恐，叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: Xing, in terror, kowtowed and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, in terror, kowtowed and confessed.

sentences.zh: 法當死，太后原之。
