translations.literal: By law he deserved death; the Empress Dowager pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: By law he deserved death, but the Empress Dowager pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 二月，流行嶺南，在道，為仇家所殺。

translations.literal: Second month, he was exiled to Lingnan; on the road he was killed by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was exiled to Lingnan and was killed on the road by an enemy of his family.

sentences.zh: 興與索元禮、來俊臣競為暴刻，興、元禮所殺各數千人，俊臣所破千餘家。

translations.literal: Xing, Suo Yuanli, and Lai Jun Chen competed in cruelty; Xing and Yuanli each killed several thousand people, and Jun Chen ruined more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Suo Yuanli, and Lai Jun Chen vied in cruelty. Xing and Yuanli each killed several thousand people, and Jun Chen destroyed more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 元禮殘酷尤甚，太后亦殺之以慰人望。

translations.literal: Yuanli was especially cruel; the Empress Dowager also killed him to satisfy public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was especially cruel, and the Empress Dowager had him killed as well to satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 徙左衛大將軍千乘王武攸暨為定王。

translations.literal: Left Guard Grand General Prince of Qiansheng Wu Youji was transferred to be Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youji, Grand General of the Left Guard and Prince of Qiansheng, was transferred to be Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 立故太子賢之子光順為義豐王。

translations.literal: The former Crown Prince Xian's son Guangshun was established as Prince of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshun, son of the former Crown Prince Xian, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太后命始祖墓曰德陵，睿祖墓曰喬陵，嚴祖墓曰節陵，肅祖墓曰簡陵，烈祖墓曰靖陵，顯祖墓曰永陵，改章德陵為昊陵，顯義陵為順陵。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Empress Dowager named the Founding Ancestor's tomb Deling, the Sagacious Ancestor's tomb Qiaoling, the Stern Ancestor's tomb Jieling, the Reverent Ancestor's tomb Jianling, the Fierce Ancestor's tomb Jingling, and the Illustrious Ancestor's tomb Yongling; Zhang Deling was changed to Haoling and Xian Yiling to Shunling.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Empress Dowager named the Founding Ancestor's tomb Deling, the Sagacious Ancestor's Qiaoling, the Stern Ancestor's Jieling, the Reverent Ancestor's Jianling, the Fierce Ancestor's Jingling, and the Illustrious Ancestor's Yongling; Zhang Deling was renamed Haoling and Xian Yiling was renamed Shunling.

sentences.zh: 追復李君羨官爵。

translations.literal: Li Junxian's office and rank were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: The offices and rank of Li Junxian were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the new moon of renyin, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of the renyin day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，制以釋教開革命之階，升於道教之上。

translations.literal: On guimao, a decree placed Buddhism, which opened the path to dynastic change, above Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao a decree placed Buddhism — which had opened the path to dynastic change — above Daoism.

sentences.zh: 命建安王攸宜留守長安。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Youyi was ordered to remain and guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Youyi was ordered to remain at Chang'an as regent.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，鑄大鐘，置北闕。

translations.literal: On bingchen, a great bell was cast and placed at the northern gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen a great bell was cast and placed at the northern gate-tower.

sentences.zh: 五月，以岑長倩為武威道行軍大總管，擊吐蕃，中道召還，軍竟不出。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Cen Changqian was made grand commander of the campaign army on the Wuwei Circuit to attack the Tibetans; midway he was recalled, and in the end the army never marched out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Cen Changqian was appointed grand commander of the campaign army on the Wuwei Circuit to attack the Tibetans, but he was recalled midway and the army never marched.

sentences.zh: 六月，以左肅政大夫格輔元為地官尚書，與鸞台侍郎樂思晦、鳳閣侍郎任知古並同平章事。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Left Director of the Bureau for Scrutiny Ge Fuyuan was made Minister of Territorial Administration, and together with Crane Terrace Vice Minister Yue Sihui and Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Ren Zhigu all became Co-equal Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Ge Fuyuan, Left Director of the Bureau for Scrutiny, was made Minister of Territorial Administration; Yue Sihui, Vice Minister of the Crane Terrace, and Ren Zhigu, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, were all made Co-equal Chancellors as well.

sentences.zh: 思晦，彥□之子也。

translations.literal: Sihui was a son of Yan [character missing in source].
translations.idiomatic: Sihui was the son of Yan [character missing in the source].

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，徙關內戶數十萬以實洛陽。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, several hundred thousand households of Guannei were moved to fill out Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, several hundred thousand households from Guannei were relocated to populate Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊申，納言武攸寧罷為左羽林大將軍；

translations.literal: Eighth month, on wushen, Master of Appeals Wu Youning was dismissed and made Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wushen, Wu Youning, Master of Appeals, was dismissed and made Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard;

sentences.zh: 夏官尚書歐陽通為司禮卿兼判納言事。

translations.literal: Minister of the Summer Office Ouyang Tong was made Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently acting Master of Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Tong, Minister of the Summer Office, was made Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently acting Master of Appeals.

sentences.zh: 庚申，殺玉鈐衛大將軍張虔勖。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Jade Talisman Guard Grand General Zhang Qianxu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Zhang Qianxu, Grand General of the Jade Talisman Guard, was executed.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣鞫虔勖獄，虔勖自訟於徐有功；

translations.literal: Lai Jun Chen interrogated the Zhang Qianxu case; Qianxu pleaded his own case before Xu Yougong;
translations.idiomatic: Lai Jun Chen interrogated the Zhang Qianxu case, and Qianxu pleaded his case before Xu Yougong;

sentences.zh: 俊臣怒，命衛士以刀亂斫殺之，梟首於市。

translations.literal: Jun Chen, in anger, ordered guards to hack him to death with swords in disorder, and his head was displayed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Chen, enraged, ordered guards to hack him to death and displayed his head in the market.

sentences.zh: 義豐王光順、嗣雍王守禮、永安王守義、長信縣主等皆賜姓武氏，與睿宗諸子皆幽閉宮中，不出門庭者十餘年。

translations.literal: Prince of Yifeng Guangshun, Prince of Siyong Shouli, Prince of Yong'an Shouyi, the Princess of Changxin, and others were all granted the surname Wu; together with the sons of Emperor Ruizong they were all confined within the palace and did not leave the gate or courtyard for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshun, Prince of Yifeng, Shouli, Prince of Siyong, Shouyi, Prince of Yong'an, the Princess of Changxin, and others were all granted the surname Wu. Together with the sons of Emperor Ruizong they were confined within the palace and did not cross the gate or courtyard for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 守禮、守義，光順之弟也。

translations.literal: Shouli and Shouyi were younger brothers of Guangshun.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli and Shouyi were Guangshun's younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 或告地官尚書武思文初與徐敬業通謀；

translations.literal: Someone reported that Minister of Territorial Administration Wu Siwen had at first conspired with Xu Jingye;
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Wu Siwen, Minister of Territorial Administration, had at first conspired with Xu Jingye;

sentences.zh: 甲子，流思文於嶺南，複姓徐氏。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Siwen was exiled to Lingnan and his surname was restored to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Siwen was exiled to Lingnan and his surname was restored to Xu.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙亥，殺岐州刺史雲弘嗣。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on yihai, Prefect of Qi Prefecture Yun Hongsi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yihai, Yun Hongsi, prefect of Qi Prefecture, was executed.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣鞫之，不問一款，先斷其首，乃偽立案奏之。

translations.literal: Lai Jun Chen interrogated him; without asking a single article of charge, he first cut off his head, then fabricated a case and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Jun Chen interrogated him; without a single question he first cut off his head, then fabricated a case and memorialized it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其殺張虔勖亦然。

translations.literal: His killing of Zhang Qianxu was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He had done the same in killing Zhang Qianxu.

sentences.zh: 敕旨皆依，海內鉗口。

translations.literal: Imperial orders all followed his reports; within the four seas mouths were clamped shut.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders approved every report, and throughout the realm people clamped their mouths shut.

sentences.zh: 鸞台侍郎、同平章事傅遊藝夢登湛露殿，以語所親，所親告之；

translations.literal: Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor Fu Youyi dreamed that he ascended the Zhanlu Hall and told those close to him; those close to him reported it;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youyi, Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor, dreamed that he ascended the Zhanlu Hall and told those close to him, who reported it;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，下獄，自殺。

translations.literal: On renchen, he was thrown into prison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he was imprisoned and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左羽林衛大將軍建昌王武攸寧為納言，洛州司馬狄仁傑為地官侍郎，與冬官侍郎裴行本並同平章事。

translations.literal: On guisi, Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning was made Master of Appeals; Luozhou Assistant Commander Di Renjie was made Vice Minister of Territorial Administration, and together with Winter Office Vice Minister Pei Xingben all became Co-equal Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Wu Youning, Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard and Prince of Jianchang, was made Master of Appeals; Di Renjie, Assistant Commander of Luozhou, was made Vice Minister of Territorial Administration; and Pei Xingben, Vice Minister of the Winter Office, was also made Co-equal Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太后謂仁傑曰：「卿在汝南，甚有善政，卿欲知譖卿者名乎！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said to Renjie: "When you were in Runan you had very good governance. Do you wish to know the name of the one who slandered you?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said to Renjie, "When you were in Runan you governed very well. Would you like to know the name of the one who slandered you?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑謝曰：「陛下以臣為過，臣請改之；

translations.literal: Renjie thanked her and said: "If Your Majesty holds your subject at fault, your subject asks to reform;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied, "If Your Majesty finds fault in me, I ask to reform;

sentences.zh: 知臣無過，臣之幸也，不願知譖者名。」

translations.literal: if Your Majesty knows your subject is without fault, that is your subject's good fortune — he does not wish to know the slander's name."
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty knows I am without fault, that is my good fortune — I do not wish to know the slander's name."

sentences.zh: 太后深歎美之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sighed deeply in admiration.

sentences.zh: 先是，鳳閣舍人修武張嘉福使洛陽人王慶之等數百人上表，請立武承嗣為皇太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Zhang Jiafu of Xiuwu had several hundred men of Luoyang including Wang Qingzhi submit a memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Jiafu of Xiuwu, Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, had several hundred men of Luoyang including Wang Qingzhi submit a memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be made Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品岑長倩以皇嗣在東宮，不宜有此議，奏請切責上書者，告示令散。

translations.literal: Wenchang Palace Right Chancellor Cen Changqian, Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, because the imperial heir was in the Eastern Palace, held that there should not be such a proposal; he memorialized asking that the memorializers be sternly rebuked and publicly ordered to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Changqian, Right Chancellor of the Wenchang Palace and Co-equal with the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, held that with the imperial heir already in the Eastern Palace such a proposal was improper; he memorialized asking that the petitioners be sternly rebuked and ordered to disperse.

sentences.zh: 太后又問地官尚書、同平章事格輔元，輔元固稱不可。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager also asked Minister of Territorial Administration and Co-equal Chancellor Ge Fuyuan; Fuyuan firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager also asked Ge Fuyuan, Minister of Territorial Administration and Co-equal Chancellor; Fuyuan firmly said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 由是大忤諸武意，故斥長倩令西征吐蕃，未至，征還，下制獄。

translations.literal: Because of this they greatly offended the Wu faction; therefore Changqian was sent away to campaign west against the Tibetans, recalled before he arrived, and thrown into the special prison.
translations.idiomatic: This greatly offended the Wu faction. Changqian was therefore sent to campaign west against the Tibetans, recalled before he arrived, and thrown into the special prison.

sentences.zh: 承嗣又譖輔元。

translations.literal: Chengsi also slandered Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi also brought false charges against Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣又脅長倩子靈原，令引司禮卿兼判納言事歐陽通等數十人，皆雲同反。

translations.literal: Lai Jun Chen also coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan to implicate Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently acting Master of Appeals Ouyang Tong and several dozen others, all saying they rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Jun Chen also coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan into implicating Ouyang Tong, Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently acting Master of Appeals, and several dozen others, all as co-conspirators in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 通為俊臣所訊，五毒備至，終無異詞，俊臣乃詐為通款。

translations.literal: Tong was interrogated by Jun Chen; the five poisons were all applied, yet in the end he had no differing words; Jun Chen then falsely made a confession in Tong's name.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was interrogated by Jun Chen; every torture was applied, yet he never changed his testimony. Jun Chen then forged a confession in Tong's name.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，長倩、輔元、通等皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jiyou, Changqian, Fuyuan, Tong, and others were all executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou Changqian, Fuyuan, Tong, and the others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 王慶之見太后，太后曰：「皇嗣我子，奈何廢之？」

translations.literal: Wang Qingzhi saw the Empress Dowager; the Empress Dowager said: "The imperial heir is my son — how could he be deposed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qingzhi saw the Empress Dowager, she said, "The imperial heir is my son — how could I depose him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「『神不歆非類，民不祀非族。』

translations.literal: He replied: "'Spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind; the people do not sacrifice to those not of their clan.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "'Spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind; the people do not sacrifice to those not of their clan.

sentences.zh: 今誰有天下，而以李氏為嗣乎！」

translations.literal: Who now holds all under Heaven, yet would make the Li clan the heirs!"
translations.idiomatic: Who now holds all under Heaven, yet would make the Li clan the heirs!"

sentences.zh: 太后諭遣之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager instructed him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager instructed him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 慶之伏地，以死泣請，不去。

translations.literal: Qingzhi prostrated himself and, weeping, begged as if for his life, and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi prostrated himself and, weeping as if for his life, begged to stay and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 太后乃以印紙遺之曰：「欲見我，以此示門者。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then gave him stamped paper and said: "If you wish to see me, show this to the gatekeepers."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then gave him a stamped pass and said, "If you wish to see me, show this to the gatekeepers."

sentences.zh: 自是慶之屢求見，太后頗怒之，命鳳閣侍郎李昭德賜慶之杖。

translations.literal: From then on Qingzhi repeatedly asked to see her; the Empress Dowager was quite angry and ordered Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Li Zhaode to bestow the beating staff on Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Qingzhi repeatedly asked to see her. The Empress Dowager grew angry and ordered Li Zhaode, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, to beat Qingzhi with the staff.

sentences.zh: 昭德引出光政門外，以示朝士曰：「此賊欲廢我皇嗣，立武承嗣！」

translations.literal: Zhaode led him out beyond the Guangzheng Gate and showed him to the court gentlemen, saying: "This villain wishes to depose our imperial heir and establish Wu Chengsi!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode led him out beyond the Guangzheng Gate and showed him to the court gentlemen, saying, "This villain wishes to depose our imperial heir and establish Wu Chengsi!"

sentences.zh: 命撲之，耳目皆血出，然後杖殺之，其黨乃散。

translations.literal: He ordered him beaten until blood poured from his ears and eyes, then beaten to death with the staff; only then did his faction disperse.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him beaten until blood poured from his ears and eyes, then beaten to death with the staff; only then did his faction disperse.

sentences.zh: 昭德因言於太后曰：「天皇，陛下之夫；

translations.literal: Zhaode then said to the Empress Dowager: "The Heavenly Emperor was Your Majesty's husband;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode then said to the Empress Dowager, "The Heavenly Emperor was your husband;

sentences.zh: 皇嗣，陛下之子。

translations.literal: the imperial heir is Your Majesty's son.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial heir is your son.

sentences.zh: 陛下身有天下，當傳之子孫為萬代業，豈得以侄為嗣乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally holds all under Heaven — you should transmit it to sons and grandsons as the enterprise of ten thousand generations. How could you take a nephew as heir!
translations.idiomatic: You personally hold all under Heaven — you should transmit it to sons and grandsons as an enterprise for ten thousand generations. How could you take a nephew as heir!

sentences.zh: 自古未聞侄為天子而為姑立廟者也！

translations.literal: From antiquity one has never heard of a nephew becoming Son of Heaven yet erecting a temple for his aunt!
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity one has never heard of a nephew becoming emperor yet erecting a temple for his aunt!

sentences.zh: 且陛下受天皇顧托，若以天下與承嗣，則天皇不血食矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty received the Heavenly Emperor's deathbed entrustment — if you give all under Heaven to Chengsi, then the Heavenly Emperor will receive no blood offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you received the Heavenly Emperor's deathbed entrustment — if you give the realm to Chengsi, the Heavenly Emperor will receive no blood offerings.

sentences.zh: 太后亦以為然。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager also thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 昭德，乾祐之子也。

translations.literal: Zhaode was a son of Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode was the son of Qianyou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，殺鸞台侍郎、同平章事樂思晦、右衛將軍李安靜。

translations.literal: On renchen, Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor Yue Sihui and Right Guard General Li Anjing were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Yue Sihui, Crane Terrace Vice Minister and Co-equal Chancellor, and Li Anjing, General of the Right Guard, were executed.

sentences.zh: 安靜，綱之孫也。

translations.literal: Anjing was a grandson of Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Anjing was the grandson of Gang.

sentences.zh: 太后將革命，王公百官皆上表勸進，安靜獨正色拒之。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager was about to change the dynasty, princes, dukes, and the hundred officials all submitted memorials urging her accession; Anjing alone, with stern countenance, refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager was about to seize the throne, princes, dukes, and all the officials submitted memorials urging her accession; Anjing alone, with stern countenance, refused.

sentences.zh: 及下制獄，來俊臣詰其反狀，安靜曰：「以我唐家老臣，須殺即殺！

translations.literal: When he was thrown into the special prison, Lai Jun Chen questioned him about the facts of rebellion; Anjing said: "As an old minister of the Tang house, if you must kill, then kill!
translations.idiomatic: When he was thrown into the special prison, Lai Jun Chen questioned him about treason. Anjing said, "As an old minister of the Tang house, if you must kill me, then kill!

sentences.zh: 若問謀反，實無可對！」

translations.literal: If you ask about plotting rebellion, in truth there is nothing to answer!"
translations.idiomatic: If you ask about plotting rebellion, I have nothing to answer!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣竟殺之。

translations.literal: Jun Chen in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Chen killed him in the end.

sentences.zh: 太學生王循之上表，乞假還鄉，太后許之。

translations.literal: The Imperial University student Wang Xunzhi submitted a memorial requesting leave to return home; the Empress Dowager granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xunzhi, a student at the Imperial University, petitioned for leave to visit his home village, and the Empress Dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑曰：「臣聞君人者唯殺生之柄不假人，自餘皆歸之有司。

translations.literal: Di Renjie said: "I have heard that for one who rules men, only the power over life and death is not lent to others; all the rest is returned to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie said, "A ruler, I have heard, should keep the power of life and death in his own hands alone. Everything else belongs to the proper offices of government.

sentences.zh: 故左、右丞，徒以下不句；

translations.literal: Therefore the left and right assistant commissioners do not pass final judgment on cases of penal servitude and below;
translations.idiomatic: That is why the left and right assistant commissioners do not decide cases punishable by penal servitude or less.

sentences.zh: 左、右相，流以上乃判，為其漸貴故也。

translations.literal: the left and right prime ministers pass judgment only from exile upward — because of the gradual increase in dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right chancellors judge only exile and heavier penalties, for the gravity of the office rises step by step.

sentences.zh: 彼學生求假，丞、簿事耳，若天子為之發敕，則天下之事幾敕可盡乎！

translations.literal: That student's request for leave is a matter for the assistant commissioner and registrar — if the Son of Heaven issues an edict for it, how many edicts could exhaust all affairs under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: A student's leave is business for a registrar or assistant commissioner. If the Son of Heaven must issue an edict for every such thing, how many edicts would it take to govern the world!

sentences.zh: 必欲不違其願，請普為立制而已。」

translations.literal: If you must not go against his wish, please simply establish a general regulation for all."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to honor his request without exception, establish a general rule for everyone and be done with it."

sentences.zh: 太后善之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager thought well of his advice.
